issues.body: ### Terms and Conditions - [x] I agree to the [Grant Agreement](https://9ba4718c-5c73-47c3-a024-4fc4e5278803.usrfiles.com/ugd/9ba471_6ff6db4095fd4c4ba21babec361e927e.pdf) terms if funded - [x] I agree to [Provide KYC information](https://9ba4718c-5c73-47c3-a024-4fc4e5278803.usrfiles.com/ugd/9ba471_7d9e73d16b584a61bae92282b208efc4.pdf) if funded above $50,000 USD - [x] I agree to disclose conflicts of interest - [x] I understand that this grant program is only eligible for completed work, as it is a retroactive grant program. Applications for planned or partially completed work will not be considered. All completed work will be verified and accepted by its intended users or their representatives, who will confirm that the outputs meet the required quality, functionality, and usability before the work is listed as an option for Coinholder voting. - [x] I agree that for any new open-source software, I will create a CONTRIBUTING.md file that reflects the high standards of Zcash development, using the [`librustzcash` style guides](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#styleguides) as a primary reference. - [x] I understand when contributing to existing Zcash code, I am required to adhere to the project specific contribution guidelines, paying close attention to any [merge](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#merge-workflow), [branch](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#branch-history), [pull request](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-review), and [commit](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages) guidelines as exemplified in the librustzcash repository. - [x] I understand all grants are valued in USD but will be disbursed in Shielded ZEC. I acknowledge and accept that disbursement amounts may fluctuate based on the ZEC/USD exchange rate at the time of payment. ### Application Owners (@octocat, @octocat1) @BitFalco21 ### Organization or Individual Name ShieldedScan ### Additional Team Members ```team-members.yaml None ``` ### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program? On X ### Requested Grant Amount (USD) $10,000 ### Category Infrastructure ### Project Summary ShieldedScan (shieldedscan.xyz) is a fully open-source, cypherpunk-style Zcash explorer and analytics platform with a public keyless API, the first Zcash MCP server, an AI assistant (Zeno) running on a TEE on NEAR AI, and a daily open dataset on Hugging Face. It covers blocks, transactions and addresses, the shielded pools, supply and the NSM, cross-chain swaps, mining and the node network, with original analytics charts built on its own full index of the chain, and is used by third-party projects such as ShieldedFlow X account, OpenZcash's agent and Zcash Names. ### Project Description **What it is** ShieldedScan (shieldedscan.xyz) is a fully open-source (AGPL-3.0), cypherpunk-style Zcash explorer and analytics platform. It runs on its own archive node, its own full index of the chain from genesis, and its own network crawler, so every figure it publishes comes from the chain itself and can be checked. **What it covers** - **Explorer:** blocks, transactions, transparent addresses, unified addresses (showing the receivers each one contains), the mempool, observed reorgs and the orphan rate, and Zcash Names (ZNS) lookups. - **Shielded pools:** each pool's balance over time, value crossing in and out, Orchard migrating into Ironwood, notes added to each pool, and supply including the NSM. - **Cross-chain:** swaps into and out of ZEC through NEAR Intents, THORChain and Maya, by chain, venue and direction. - **Mining:** blocks, reward and fees by mining pool, how many pools mine 51% of each month's blocks, and how fresh each pool's blocks are on arrival, with pool attribution checked against the pools' own coinbase markers and block lists back to 2016. - **Network:** a live map of the nodes the crawler reaches, their client software, hosting, and readiness for network upgrades such as NU7. - **Analytics:** a library of 37 charts, including original ones such as transparent coin age, ZEC held on labelled exchange addresses, and issuance against NSM removals. - **Testnet:** a full testnet explorer at testnet.shieldedscan.xyz. - **Automated alerts on X:** @shieldedscanxyz posts a daily chain snapshot, plus an alert for every large cross-chain swap into or out of ZEC and every large shielding or unshielding, each with an image card and the transaction hash. - **Learn:** an interactive guide (shieldedscan.xyz/learn) that takes a newcomer from no ZEC to a first shielded transaction: a practice mode with a simulated exchange, wallet and chain, narrated by Zeno, and a real mode that checks each of the reader's own steps on the chain. Built for the ZECATHON hackathon in October 2026. - **And more:** a live view of the chain's flows (/pulse), the halving countdown, a rich list of transparent addresses, a ZEC price and stats page, a market-cap comparison with other coins, the cost of mining one ZEC in each country, a map of the Zcash ecosystem, a fact-check page on common claims about Zcash, an index of every ZIP, and Satoshi's Lock, a slot machine where each pull is a real attempt at the Bitcoin genesis key. **Open data and access** - **Open source:** the whole stack is open source under AGPL-3.0 at github.com/BitFalco21/shieldedscan. That includes the front-end, the API, the chain indexer, the network crawler and the open-data exporter. - **Public API:** a keyless API with 58 documented endpoints. Everything the site shows is available there. - **MCP server:** the first Zcash MCP server, with 35 tools, so any AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and others) can query the chain directly. - **Zeno:** an AI assistant on the site that answers questions from the same data, can draw a chart under its answer, and can hand over the underlying data as a CSV or JSON file. It runs on a TEE on NEAR AI. - **Open dataset:** a daily dataset on Hugging Face with 34 tables and 13.8 GB, including the full transaction history and the transparent ledger. - **Self-hosting:** documented, so anyone can run their own copy of the explorer from the open code and data. **Goals** - Make Zcash's public data easy to read, use and verify, for users, researchers, developers and AI agents. - Show how the shielded pools are actually used: balances, flows between pools, how many notes each pool holds (the crowd a shielded spend hides in), and how value moves across the shielded boundary. - Keep it open: open code, an open API and open data, so the work stays useful to the ecosystem whatever happens to this project. - Be reliable infrastructure that other projects can build on. ShieldedFlow, OpenZcash's agent and Zcash Names already do. ### Technical Approach (how you did it) **Architecture** - **Own node:** ShieldedScan runs its own Zcash archive node, Zakura, currently v1.7.0, for both mainnet and testnet. All chain data comes from our own copy of the chain; no third-party explorer is used for it. - **Chain index:** a follower reads each new block from the node and writes it into PostgreSQL: blocks, transactions, every transparent input and output, per-pool value balances and note counts. The full history from genesis was backfilled in July 2026: about 18 million transactions and 350 million transparent inputs and outputs. - **Analytics:** daily and monthly series (pool balances, flows, fees, mining, supply) are kept as rollup tables, updated incrementally every 10 minutes from the blocks that changed. Larger datasets (coin age, exchange-address balances, block arrival times, per-address transaction counts) are filled by background trackers paced so they never slow down ingestion. - **API:** a read-only TypeScript service (Hono on Node.js). It serves the website and the public keyless API, behind per-IP rate limits, on separate processes so heavy public traffic can't slow down the site. - **External sources:** pollers for NEAR Intents, THORChain and Maya bring in cross-chain swaps; prices come from CoinGecko and Kraken. Our own peer-to-peer crawler maps the reachable nodes over IPv4 and IPv6. - **Front-end:** Next.js and TypeScript in strict mode, with Tailwind. All charts are hand-written SVG, with no chart library. It is hosted on Netlify behind Cloudflare and builds from the public repository. - **MCP server:** a stateless implementation of the MCP protocol. Its tools are generated from the same catalogue that renders the API documentation, so the docs, the API and the MCP server can't disagree. - **Zeno:** an AI assistant that answers by calling the same public API, so it can only state figures the API serves. It runs on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash inside a TEE on NEAR AI Cloud, and is held to an evaluation suite of over 200 questions, including prompt-injection attempts. - **Open dataset:** a daily export at 04:40 UTC turns the index into Parquet files on Hugging Face. Each release is checked against the previous one, so already-published history can't change silently. A self-hosting guide imports the dataset into a working copy of the explorer. **Process** - **Code review:** every change goes through a pull request on GitHub, with automated checks (type checking, lint, about 5,800 unit tests, database tests on a real PostgreSQL, end-to-end browser tests, secret scanning and image builds) before it can merge. - **Verified figures:** the main figures are reconciled against the node before they ship. For example, pool balances, supply and the coin-age bands all match the node's own value pools exactly, down to the smallest unit. - **Deploys:** the API ships before the front-end, old versions are kept for instant rollback, and ingestion never stops during a deploy. - **Monitoring:** an automated check runs every minute and alerts the maintainer (me) on Telegram if the API slows down or fails, indexing falls behind the node, the node stops answering, the disk fills up or the homepage stops updating, with a recovery message and a daily summary. - **Upgrades:** NU7 support was tested on testnet first, where its activation was followed live. **Key dates (2026)** - **July:** explorer launched on our own node and index; full history backfilled. - **August:** public keyless API (August 1), testnet explorer (August 5), Zeno live (August 28). - **September:** network crawler and node map. - **October:** MCP server (October 4), source code published under AGPL-3.0 (v1.0.0, October 8), Zcash Names integration, NU7 readiness tracking. - **November:** open dataset on Hugging Face (November 1), completed with the full transparent ledger and self-hosting (November 8); nine new analytics charts and incremental analytics (November 9–10). ### Time Period of Work Completion July 2026 - November 2026 ### Total Budget (USD) $10,000 ### Budget Breakdown **Compensation:** - $(USD): 9,731 - Justification: product decisions, design, development, data verification, operations, marketing on social media (posts, community engagement, infographics, videos) and maintenance of ShieldedScan from July to November 2026: the explorer, chain index, public API, MCP server, Zeno, network crawler, open dataset and self-hosting, plus running the infrastructure (node upgrades, deploys, monitoring). **Technology/Software:** - $(USD): 0 - Justification: The software is open source; no paid licences. **Infrastructure/Hosting:** - $(USD): 269 - Justification: Dedicated server with local block storage for the archive nodes, database, API and crawler at about $36/month from late July 2026 (4 months, $144), and front-end hosting at about $20/month for July to November 2026 (5 months, $100). $15/year for the domain registration. $10 in credits on NEAR AI for running Zeno. **Services/Contractors:** - $(USD): 0 - Justification: None. All development and operations are handled by me. No contractors, agencies or paid data providers. **Other:** - $(USD): 0 - Justification: No other costs. Total $(USD): 10,000 ### Previous Funding No ### Previous Funding Details N/A ### Other Funding Sources Yes ### Other Funding Sources Details Donations from community members. ### Success Metrics **Adoption by other Zcash projects** - ShieldedFlow links to ShieldedScan on its X account automated posts (1600+ followers) and its Telegram bot. https://x.com/ShieldedFlow - OpenZcash's agent (Zarvis) uses ShieldedScan's data to answer questions about Zcash. https://openzcash.org/zarvis - Zcash Names (ZNS): ShieldedScan is an official partner and resolves names on the explorer. ZNS has highlighted it publicly. https://x.com/ZcashNames/status/2106812092598943951 - hidn_room uses ShieldedScan's supply data. https://hidnroom.com/ **Open data in use** - The Hugging Face dataset has been public since November 1, 2026, updated daily. It has 34 tables and 13.8 GB, including the full transaction history and the transparent ledger. - The public API has 58 keyless endpoints, and the MCP server has 35 tools. There are no accounts or keys at all: anyone can use them, and no one has to identify themselves. - The full source code is public under AGPL-3.0, with a self-hosting guide, so the work stays available to the ecosystem. - The agent Zeno has answered 200+ questions since August 2026, with no account needed and no question logged. **Analytics** - **Charts:** a library of 37 analytics charts. (e.g. transparent coin age, ZEC held on labelled exchange addresses, issuance against NSM removals, block arrival times by mining pool, and node software and hosting over time.) - **Mining history:** pool attribution back to 2016, each pool identified by the name it writes into its own blocks or by the block list on its own website. - **NU7 readiness:** tracked for the network, with a public chart of which reachable nodes run a release that can follow it, and testnet activation followed live. **Automated bot:** - @shieldedscanxyz on X: an automated feed of 941 posts since late August 2026: daily chain snapshots, cross-chain swap alerts and shielding/unshielding alerts, all generated from the explorer's own data. ### Proof of completion **Repository/Commit:** - [Repository](https://github.com/BitFalco21/shieldedscan) - The full source code (front-end, API, chain indexer, network crawler, open-data exporter) under AGPL-3.0, with a CONTRIBUTING.md and a security policy. - [Self-hosting guide](https://github.com/BitFalco21/shieldedscan/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md) - How to run your own copy of the explorer from the open code and dataset. **Publication:** - [Open dataset on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Shieldedscanxyz/zcash-mainnet) - 34 tables and 13.8 GB, including the full transaction history and the transparent ledger, refreshed daily since November 1, 2026. - [API documentation](https://shieldedscan.xyz/api-docs) - 58 keyless endpoints, each with an example and a "try it" button. **Deployment/Release:** - [shieldedscan.xyz](https://shieldedscan.xyz/) - The live mainnet explorer. - [testnet.shieldedscan.xyz](https://testnet.shieldedscan.xyz/) - The live testnet explorer. - [Public API](https://api.shieldedscan.xyz/v1) - The live keyless API. - [MCP server](https://shieldedscan.xyz/mcp) - The MCP server, with setup steps for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and VS Code. - [Zeno](https://shieldedscan.xyz/ai-agent) - The AI assistant, running inside a TEE on NEAR AI. ### Conflict of Interest Disclosure No actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest. ### Community Forum Posting - [x] I understand it is my responsibility to post a link to this issue on the [Zcash Community Forums](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/about-the-retroactive-grants-category/52106) after this application has been submitted so the community can give input. I understand this is required in order for the community to discuss and vote on this grant application. Note: If you are unable to post on the forum (for example, due to new user restrictions), please leave a comment below, and we will adjust your posting permissions.

issues.body:
### Terms and Conditions

- [x] I agree to the [Grant Agreement](https://9ba4718c-5c73-47c3-a024-4fc4e5278803.usrfiles.com/ugd/9ba471_6ff6db4095fd4c4ba21babec361e927e.pdf) terms if funded
- [x] I agree to [Provide KYC information](https://9ba4718c-5c73-47c3-a024-4fc4e5278803.usrfiles.com/ugd/9ba471_7d9e73d16b584a61bae92282b208efc4.pdf) if funded above $50,000 USD
- [x] I agree to disclose conflicts of interest
- [x] I understand that this grant program is only eligible for completed work, as it is a retroactive grant program. Applications for planned or partially completed work will not be considered. All completed work will be verified and accepted by its intended users or their representatives, who will confirm that the outputs meet the required quality, functionality, and usability before the work is listed as an option for Coinholder voting.
- [x] I agree that for any new open-source software, I will create a CONTRIBUTING.md file that reflects the high standards of Zcash development, using the [`librustzcash` style guides](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#styleguides) as a primary reference.
- [x] I understand when contributing to existing Zcash code, I am required to adhere to the project specific contribution guidelines, paying close attention to any [merge](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#merge-workflow), [branch](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#branch-history), [pull request](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-review), and [commit](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages) guidelines as exemplified in the librustzcash repository.
- [x] I understand all grants are valued in USD but will be disbursed in Shielded ZEC. I acknowledge and accept that disbursement amounts may fluctuate based on the ZEC/USD exchange rate at the time of payment.

### Application Owners (@octocat, @octocat1)

@Adeolu05

### Organization or Individual Name

David Peluola (individual, solo)

### Additional Team Members

```team-members.yaml
None. Community research credited on the site (wallet and exchange claims) came from orb, a Zcash community member, as a volunteer. The code was written with an AI coding assistant (Anthropic's Claude) under my direction: I designed the features, ran the tests and on-chain checks, and reviewed and deployed every change.
```

### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

The Zcash Community Forum, Retroactive Grants category, and FPF's post with the 2026 round dates.

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

4817

### Category

Infrastructure

### Project Summary

Can I Shield? (https://canishield.vercel.app) is a live, open-source board that answers "can I send shielded ZEC to this service, and will a shielded deposit be credited?" for 40 exchanges, wallets, hardware wallets and swaps, with every answer backed by checkable evidence. In October and November 2026 it added NU7 readiness tooling and shielded deposit checks, and recorded the first verified post-NU7 shielded deposit to Binance.

### Project Description

Zcash users who hold shielded funds often cannot tell in advance whether an exchange or wallet will accept a unified address, pay out to a shielded address, or credit a deposit that came from the shielded pool. The answers are scattered across support pages, old forum threads and word of mouth, and many are out of date. A failed send costs fees and time and pushes people back to transparent addresses.

Can I Shield? collects those answers in one place and labels each one by how strong its evidence is, so a reader never confuses a claim with a proof:

1. **On-chain verified tests.** A service pays a test address the project controls. A scanner confirms which pool the money landed in, and the page publishes the txid, block and a viewing key so anyone can check it.
2. **Shielded deposit checks** (new this quarter). A tester sends a small, unique amount from a shielded wallet to their own deposit address at a service. The scanner verifies the payment on-chain, including two-step TEX payments (ZIP 320). The tester then reports whether and when it was credited, and a maintainer reviews a screenshot before anything is published.
3. **Community reports.** Withdrawal-form checks: an address type pasted into a service's withdrawal form, with a screenshot. Nothing is sent and no keys are used.
4. **Listings and research.** Claims from the ZecHub Wiki (28 listings) and community research by orb (38 claims), always labelled as unverified.

**Work completed this period:**

- **The board and evidence model** (30 Sep to 11 Oct 2026). 40 mainnet services (16 exchanges, 17 wallets, 4 hardware wallets, 3 swaps), Ironwood readiness verdicts, staleness rules, service pages, a JSON export (`/api/results.json`) and link previews. Submitted to Colosseum's Crypto World's Fair, Zcash track, on 11 Oct.
- **NU7 readiness page** (29 Oct). A live countdown, what to do by role (wallet users, old Sprout holders, people who withdraw from exchanges, node and explorer operators), what changes, with sources, then a live chain strip and an activation record once NU7 activated at block 3,543,405.
- **NU7 Stopwatch** (5 Nov). Measured block gaps before and after NU7 from the chain itself: 75.4 s average over 23,404 gaps before, 25.7 s over 5,721 gaps since. Share cards update as blocks arrive.
- **Shielded deposit checks** (built 29 Oct, opened on mainnet 7 Nov). Squirrel, head of ZecHub, asked for exactly this on ZecHub's 28 Oct community call: confirm deposits the way withdrawals are confirmed, and record the time taken.
- **First verified result** (7 Nov). A shielded deposit from Zodl Android 3.19.0 to Binance's TEX address was verified on-chain as coming from Ironwood in two steps, and Binance credited it about 8 minutes after it landed. Binance's own deposit screen warns that deposits with shielded inputs are not credited, so this answers a real question.
- **Privacy by design.** A deposit address is never stored, only its kind and a keyed hash. The exact amount, txid, block and screenshot are deleted when a check is reviewed. Public times are rounded to the nearest 5 minutes so they cannot be used to find the transaction.

### Technical Approach (how you did it)

A TypeScript monorepo (MIT), 56 commits from 30 Sep to 7 Nov 2026, with 108 automated tests:

- **Web app** (`web/`): Next.js 16 and Tailwind on Vercel. Mainnet board at `/`, testnet at `/testnet`, a page per service, the test and deposit-check flows, the NU7 page, and link-preview cards drawn per service.
- **Scanner worker** (`worker/`): runs on Railway, one per network. It reads the chain from public lightwalletd/Zaino endpoints with fallbacks (`na.zec.rocks`, `eu.zec.rocks`, `zaino.unsafe.zec.rocks` on mainnet) and stops if an endpoint is on the wrong chain. It records the pool, txid, height and memo of each test payment, and verifies deposit checks through ZecBlock's transaction API, following TEX payments one hop back to confirm the funds left the shielded pool.
- **Keys** (`keygen/`): each withdrawal test gets a throwaway key generated offline (ZIP-32, via `@ledgerhq/zcash-utils`). Only public data reaches the server, and each test's viewing key is published so anyone can re-check it. Mainnet stays off unless three separate switches are set.
- **Data** (`packages/db/`): Postgres with Drizzle migrations. Database constraints refuse a published deposit check that still holds private fields, and a credited check whose credit time comes before the payment.
- **Addresses** (`packages/zcash/`): unified address and F4Jumble encoding, and decoding for transparent, TEX, Sapling and unified deposit addresses.
- **Open data**: `GET /api/results.json` (CORS-open, results licensed CC BY 4.0) carries every verdict, test, report and published deposit check, so wallets and explorers can reuse it.

Key dates: board and scanners 30 Sep to 11 Oct; withdrawal timing 28 Oct; NU7 page and deposit checks 29 Oct; NU7 Stopwatch 5 Nov; mainnet deposit checks, first verified Binance deposit and per-service preview cards 7 Nov.

### Time Period of Work Completion

30 September 2026 to 7 November 2026

### Total Budget (USD)

4817

### Budget Breakdown

- Compensation:
  - $(USD): 4800
  - Justification: About 160 hours at $30/hour across 20 working days (30 Sep to 7 Nov 2026): spec, scanners, board, NU7 page and Stopwatch, deposit checks, testing, reviews and fixes.
- Technology/Software:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: Open-source tools only.
- Infrastructure/Hosting:
  - $(USD): 7
  - Justification: Railway Hobby plan for the Postgres database and two scanner workers: $5.00 for Oct 8 to Nov 8 plus $1.71 of usage above the included $5 (rounded to $7). Vercel Hobby and public chain endpoints were free.
- Services/Contractors:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: None; solo work.
- Other:
  - $(USD): 10
  - Justification: Mainnet test payments and network fees, including the Binance deposit check.
- Total $(USD): 4817

### Previous Funding

No

### Previous Funding Details

None.

### Other Funding Sources

No

### Other Funding Sources Details

None received for this work. Can I Shield was entered in Colosseum's Crypto World's Fair (Zcash track) on 11 Oct 2026; no prize or funding has been received, and I will disclose any later award on this issue. For transparency: I have received ZecHub bounty payouts for separate work (NU7 motion videos, an ecosystem digest and documentation), none of which paid for Can I Shield.

### Success Metrics

The value is evidence that did not exist before, published so anyone can re-check it:

- **Coverage:** 40 mainnet services tracked (16 exchanges, 17 wallets, 4 hardware wallets, 3 swaps), each with a verdict, its evidence and its date. 4 have been tested directly.
- **On-chain proof:** a verified mainnet withdrawal test (Trust Wallet pays transparent only, block 3,503,266, txid and viewing key published) and 2 verified testnet tests, including a payment that landed in Ironwood.
- **A clear finding for users:** Trust Wallet, Bitget, MEXC and Binance all rejected both Ironwood-only and full unified addresses in withdrawal-form checks (11 community reports, screenshots reviewed before publishing). None of the tested services can send shielded ZEC yet.
- **First verified shielded deposit after NU7:** Binance credited a shielded deposit from Zodl through its TEX address about 8 minutes after it landed, verified on-chain. Binance's own deposit screen warns that deposits with shielded inputs are not credited, so this answers a question users actually face.
- **Built on request:** deposit checks exist because Squirrel (ZecHub) asked for them on the 28 Oct community call; they opened on mainnet 10 days later.
- **NU7, measured:** the Stopwatch shows the change from the chain itself, 75.4 s average block gap before NU7 to 25.7 s since, with share cards for social posts.
- **Reusable:** the full dataset is an open, CORS-enabled JSON feed (CC BY 4.0) any wallet, explorer or wiki can build on, and the code is MIT.

The site runs no visitor analytics, so reach shows in public posts and reuse rather than page-view counts.

### Proof of completion

- Repository/Commit:
  - [github.com/Adeolu05/canishield](https://github.com/Adeolu05/canishield) - MIT, CONTRIBUTING.md, 56 commits, 108 tests
  - [9222be2](https://github.com/Adeolu05/canishield/commit/9222be2) and [229fa9b](https://github.com/Adeolu05/canishield/commit/229fa9b) - deposit checks: data model, address decoding, on-chain verification, tester flow and review
  - [8389a72](https://github.com/Adeolu05/canishield/commit/8389a72) and [4524658](https://github.com/Adeolu05/canishield/commit/4524658) - NU7 readiness page and live view
  - [18a9a58](https://github.com/Adeolu05/canishield/commit/18a9a58) - NU7 Stopwatch
  - [dcc85d8](https://github.com/Adeolu05/canishield/commit/dcc85d8) - withdrawal timing
  - [09af82c](https://github.com/Adeolu05/canishield/commit/09af82c) - per-service preview cards
- Deployment/Release:
  - [canishield.vercel.app](https://canishield.vercel.app) - mainnet board; [testnet board](https://canishield.vercel.app/testnet)
  - [Binance service page](https://canishield.vercel.app/services/binance) - the verified deposit result
  - [NU7 page](https://canishield.vercel.app/nu7) - readiness guide and Stopwatch
  - [Deposit check](https://canishield.vercel.app/test/deposit) - the live tester flow
  - [Open data](https://canishield.vercel.app/api/results.json) - JSON feed
- Publication:
  - [2-minute demo](https://youtu.be/dE29j72mCJM)
  - [Post on X: the verified Binance deposit](https://x.com/0xdavee_/status/2119148530358964497)
- Other Evidence:
  - Colosseum Crypto World's Fair, Zcash track, submitted 11 Oct 2026 ([project page](https://colosseum.com/arena/projects/zecproof))
  - ZecHub community call, 28 Oct 2026, where Squirrel asked for deposit checks ([recording](https://x.com/i/spaces/1nJOLQlBVbZxR))

### Conflict of Interest Disclosure

I have an inactive Bitget affiliate account (its latest report shows no referred users and no rebate income); Bitget is one of the services on the board. Its entry comes from a withdrawal-form check with a screenshot and follows the same rules as every other service. I have also received ZecHub bounty payouts for unrelated work, and Squirrel (ZecHub) suggested the deposit-check feature. I hold no role at any listed service, and no service paid for or reviewed its listing.

### Community Forum Posting

- [x] I understand it is my responsibility to post a link to this issue on the [Zcash Community Forums](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/about-the-retroactive-grants-category/52106) after this application has been submitted so the community can give input. I understand this is required in order for the community to discuss and vote on this grant application. Note: If you are unable to post on the forum (for example, due to new user restrictions), please leave a comment below, and we will adjust your posting permissions.

issues.title: Retroactive Grant Application - Independent NU7 block timing measurement, testnet and mainnet activation

### Terms and Conditions

- [x] I agree to the [Grant Agreement](https://9ba4718c-5c73-47c3-a024-4fc4e5278803.usrfiles.com/ugd/9ba471_6ff6db4095fd4c4ba21babec361e927e.pdf) terms if funded

- [x] I agree to disclose conflicts of interest
- [x] I understand that this grant program is only eligible for completed work, as it is a retroactive grant program. Applications for planned or partially completed work will not be considered. All completed work will be verified and accepted by its intended users or their representatives, who will confirm that the outputs meet the required quality, functionality, and usability before the work is listed as an option for Coinholder voting.
- [x] I agree that for any new open-source software, I will create a CONTRIBUTING.md file that reflects the high standards of Zcash development, using the [`librustzcash` style guides](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#styleguides) as a primary reference.
- [x] I understand when contributing to existing Zcash code, I am required to adhere to the project specific contribution guidelines, paying close attention to any [merge](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#merge-workflow), [branch](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#branch-history), [pull request](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-review), and [commit](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages) guidelines as exemplified in the librustzcash repository.
- [x] I understand all grants are valued in USD but will be disbursed in Shielded ZEC. I acknowledge and accept that disbursement amounts may fluctuate based on the ZEC/USD exchange rate at the time of payment.

### Application Owners (@octocat, @octocat1)

@neoalphavault-png

### Organization or Individual Name

PulseHawk (Vizora Digital UG, Germany)

### Additional Team Members

```team-members.yaml
None
```

### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

From the call for proposals in the forum on 30 Oct 2026, while we were posting our NU7 counts in the NU7 Timeline thread.

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

4500

### Category

Research & Development

### Project Summary

We counted NU7 block timing from our own header client, on testnet and around the mainnet activation on 6 Nov 2026. Before activation we published four dated forecasts with 90% bands and scored each one in public against the block. All counts, scripts and raw data are open.

### Project Description

NU7 cut the target block time from 75 s to 25 s. Wallets, exchanges and pools set confirmation counts by time, so they need to know how the new spacing behaves, measured from headers and not taken from one explorer.

What we delivered:
1. Testnet count after the NU7 testnet activation, 4 to 18 Oct 2026, 49,202 block intervals, longest gap 451 s (forum posts of 15 and 18 Oct).
2. The interval CSV of that window, published 22 Oct.
3. Four mainnet activation forecasts with 90% bands, made 23 Oct, 28 Oct, 2 Nov and 4 Nov, each from the block pace of the days before.
4. The result. Block 3,543,405 has header time 6 Nov 2026 02:34:02 UTC. It came 12 min 10 s after the 23 Oct forecast, 7 min 46 s after the 28 Oct one, 5 min 50 s before the 2 Nov one and 6 min 56 s before the 4 Nov one. All four inside their band, all four scored in public on pulsehawk.io/track-record.
5. The first 250 intervals after activation, posted in the NU7 Timeline thread on 6 Nov.
6. Upgrade report PH-UR-2026-001 for 24 h before to 72 h after activation, with heads, raw watch export, outputs and the sha256 anyone can reproduce, in github.com/pulsehawk/methods.

What node counts and explorers do not show, and this work does. A forecast published days ahead and scored against the block, block intervals counted from headers, and when a block first reached us against its header time.

### Technical Approach (how you did it)

Our own header client speaks the Zcash peer protocol and connects to several Zebra and Zakura peers. Each header is checked for proof of work and linkage before it is counted, and a second peer cross checks the hashes (500 of 500 equal on 6 Nov). Intervals use header time. A separate listener records when each block first reaches us.

Forecasts use the median block pace of the 14 days before each forecast (7 days for the 2 Nov one), with a 90% band from the spread of that pace. Counted and computed values are always labelled apart.

One gap we report openly. Our upgrade watch on our own server saw no new blocks from about 02:50 to 08:11 UTC on 6 Nov, because the DNS seeds could not be resolved from its host. The interval counts come from the header client and are not affected. The README in the methods repo says which values could miss tip switches in those hours.

Python with the standard library only. No peer addresses or host names are published.

### Time Period of Work Completion

4 Oct 2026 to 9 Nov 2026

### Total Budget (USD)

4500

### Budget Breakdown

- Compensation:
  - $(USD): 4,320
  - Justification: 60 hours of measurement, analysis, forecasts and public write ups from 4 Oct to 9 Nov 2026, at 72 USD per hour.
- Technology/Software:
  - $(USD): 150
  - Justification: share of software subscriptions and API usage for analysis and automation in October and November 2026.
- Infrastructure/Hosting:
  - $(USD): 30
  - Justification: share of our own server for the header client, listener and upgrade watch, plus domain, October and November 2026.
- Services/Contractors:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: none.
- Other:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: none.
- Total $(USD): 4,500

### Previous Funding

No

### Previous Funding Details

_No response_

### Other Funding Sources

No

### Other Funding Sources Details

No other funding was received for this work. We have offered paid measurement to Zcash node teams for future work, with no agreement so far. Any such work would cover new work only, never the items in this application.

### Success Metrics

- Four forecasts published 14 to 2 days ahead and scored in public against the block, all inside their 90% band.
- 49,202 testnet and 51,892 mainnet intervals counted and published with CSV.
- Numbers posted where the upgrade was discussed, in the NU7 Timeline thread, with method and data linked.
- Anyone can recount every number from the public scripts, the raw data and the expected sha256.

### Proof of completion

- Repository/Commit:
  - [pulsehawk/methods](https://github.com/pulsehawk/methods) - scripts, formats, testnet example and the NU7 mainnet report data with expected sha256
- Publication:
  - [Upgrade report PH-UR-2026-001](https://pulsehawk.io/reports/zcash-nu7) - 24 h before to 72 h after activation, with CSV
  - [NU7 Timeline, 15 Oct](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/nu7-timeline/57655/24) - first testnet count
  - [NU7 Timeline, 18 Oct](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/nu7-timeline/57655/26) - testnet count 4 to 18 Oct
  - [NU7 Timeline, 22 Oct](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/nu7-timeline/57655/29) - interval CSV
  - [NU7 Timeline, 30 Oct](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/nu7-timeline/57655/33) - mainnet forecast with band
  - [NU7 Timeline, 6 Nov](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/nu7-timeline/57655/35) - activation result and first 250 intervals
  - [pulsehawk.io/zcash-nu7](https://pulsehawk.io/zcash-nu7) - method, dated numbers, data
  - [pulsehawk.io/track-record](https://pulsehawk.io/track-record) - all four forecasts with band and score
- Other Evidence:
  - [X, 4 Nov](https://x.com/pulsehawkio/status/2118021706996760856) - forecast with band before activation
  - [X, 6 Nov](https://x.com/pulsehawkio/status/2118717635051343878) - activation against forecast
  - [X, 9 Nov](https://x.com/pulsehawkio/status/2119714588031889618) - all four forecasts scored

### Conflict of Interest Disclosure

PulseHawk sells independent network measurement. We hold no ZEC and take no side on NU7 or on Zcash funding questions. We have offered paid measurement for future work to Zcash node teams, with no agreement. Vizora Digital UG also runs a separate media brand about another network, which has no role in this work.

### Community Forum Posting

- [x] I understand it is my responsibility to post a link to this issue on the [Zcash Community Forums](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/about-the-retroactive-grants-category/52106) after this application has been submitted so the community can give input. I understand this is required in order for the community to discuss and vote on this grant application. Note: If you are unable to post on the forum (for example, due to new user restrictions), please leave a comment below, and we will adjust your posting permissions.

- [X] I agree that for any new open-source software, I will create a CONTRIBUTING.md file that reflects the high standards of Zcash development, using the [`librustzcash` style guides](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#styleguides) as a primary reference.

- [X] I understand all grants are valued in USD but will be disbursed in Shielded ZEC. I acknowledge and accept that disbursement amounts may fluctuate based on the ZEC/USD exchange rate at the time of payment.

### Application Owners (@octocat, @octocat1)

@kaladinlight, @gomesalexandre

### Organization or Individual Name

ShapeShift DAO

### Additional Team Members

```team-members.yaml
- Name: kaladinlight
  Role: Senior Engineer, ShapeShift DAO (current contributor)
  Responsibilities: Zcash transactions in the bitcoinjs-lib fork, native signing, Zcash indexer, chain adapter, Maya, NU6.2/NU6.3/NU7 upgrades, ZEC in the public API, widget deposit-address flow, swap-service deposit detection
- Name: gomesalexandre
  Role: ShapeShift DAO engineer Feb 2022 to Mar 2026, now at Vultisig
  Responsibilities: Ledger and Trezor signing, ZEC on NEAR Intents, production rollout and wallet gating, Blockchair fallback
- Name: NeOMakinG
  Role: ShapeShift DAO engineering, code review
  Responsibilities: reviewed the Ledger, Trezor and fallback PRs (device tests listed under Proof of completion) (web#11337, web#11338, web#11346, web#11374)
```

### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

Zcash Community Forum, Q4 2026 call for proposals.

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

$22,380

### Category

Integration

### Project Summary

ShapeShift, a free, open-source, self-custodial app, added Ledger and Trezor signing for transparent ZEC, ZEC swaps on NEAR Intents, ZEC in its public swap API and a widget you can pay by sending ZEC to a deposit address, and fixed sends after NU6.2, NU6.3 and NU7. [ZCG#81](https://github.com/ZcashCommunityGrants/zcashcommunitygrants/issues/81) paid for hosting and marketing with $0 for engineering, and its milestones are excluded here; this request prices only the engineering outside them, at cost. 311 swaps carrying ShapeShift's referral have since moved $5.85M of ZEC.

### Project Description

> **Read this first**
> - **Transparent only.** ShapeShift wallets hold and send transparent ZEC, and do not support shielded balances. October 2025 press reports of "shielded transactions" in ShapeShift overstated what exists. The widget's deposit address is transparent. You can pay it from a shielded wallet (we tested with Zodl) and our swap service finds the deposit. We refuse unified addresses as a swap destination because we have not yet proven shielded delivery through NEAR Intents.
> - **Prior grant.** [ZCG#81](https://github.com/ZcashCommunityGrants/zcashcommunitygrants/issues/81) (2025, $50,000) paid for a year of node hosting ($36,000) and marketing ($14,000), with "Compensation Costs: None". Its milestones (node, native wallet, Maya swapper, testing, go-to-market) are **excluded** from this request; see "Scope intentionally excluded". ShapeShift said it would return about $8,420 of the marketing money and we found no record that it did, so this request subtracts it.
> - **Fees.** ShapeShift takes an affiliate fee on swaps, ZEC included: $34,866 to the DAO on ZEC swaps from 5 Dec 2025 to 6 Nov 2026 (see Usage). That is more than this ask. We don't net the two: the fees fund the DAO across every chain, including the ZCG#81 milestone engineering it paid for itself, and this ask prices only engineering no grant covered.

**What ZEC users can do today**

| Capability | Where | Live since | In ZCG#81? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Balance, history, send and receive (transparent) | ShapeShift app, built-in wallet | Dec 2025 | yes, excluded |
| Signing with Ledger | hdwallet-ledger | Dec 2025 | no |
| Signing with Trezor | hdwallet-trezor | Dec 2025 | no |
| Swaps via Maya | swapper | Jan 2026 | yes, excluded |
| Swaps via NEAR Intents | swapper | Dec 2025 | no (see below) |
| Swaps via THORChain | swapper | Oct 2026 | no |
| ZEC quotes and trades for third-party integrators | public API | Jun 2026 | no |
| ZEC listed in the embeddable swap widget (signing handed to the app) | swap widget | Jun 2026 | no |
| Pay a ZEC swap by sending to a transparent deposit address, no wallet connection | widget, public API, swap-service | Sep 2026 | no |

NEAR Intents was not a [ZCG#81](https://github.com/ZcashCommunityGrants/zcashcommunitygrants/issues/81) deliverable (the proposal named only Maya). The completion post called it a bonus. We price it here.

**Usage.** From 5 Dec 2025 to 6 Nov 2026, swaps carrying ShapeShift's referral (app, API and widget) settled 311 ZEC trades worth $5.85M on the ZEC leg, and 72% of them bought ZEC. THORChain is shown apart because those swaps mostly did not come from our app (below).

| | NEAR Intents | Maya | **Total** | THORChain (apart) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Completed swaps | 246 | 65 | **311** | 55 |
| ZEC-leg volume (USD) | $3,243,413 | $2,606,143 | **$5,849,556** | $200,668 |
| Buy ZEC / sell ZEC | 172 / 74 | 52 / 13 | **224 / 87** | 53 / 2 |
| Affiliate fees received by the DAO | $19,077 | $15,789 | **$34,866** | $20 |

- The median swap is $116 and the largest $490,673 (DAI to ZEC, 9 Oct 2026). 89% of the volume came in April, July and October 2026, mostly swaps of 2 to 7 BTC into ZEC.
- 243 distinct transparent ZEC addresses took part. That is a proxy, not a user count: one person can use many addresses.
- The window starts 5 Dec 2025, three days before the production switch-on, so it includes 13 NEAR Intents swaps ($102 in all) and 2 Maya buys ($11) from before the release, most likely our own testing. They are included; without them it is 296 swaps and still $5.85M.
- THORChain swaps carry ShapeShift's `ss` affiliate at only 1 bps, far below our app's 60 bps default, and it is a secondary affiliate on three of them. The first two (3 Oct) came before the app could route ZEC on THORChain (5 Oct), and 51 of the 55 ($198K) pay out to one address on 27 and 28 Oct. They are most likely another integrator's swaps, so we leave them out of the totals.
- Swaps made through our public API and widget carry the same referral and are included.
- ZEC is 15.6% of all USD volume ShapeShift has routed through NEAR Intents since 1 Dec 2025: $3.29M of $21.08M counted on the input side (so slightly above the $3.24M ZEC-leg figure in the table), in 246 of 2,536 completed swaps (9.7%). The share swings with a few large swaps, from 2 to 12% in the other full months to 42%, 51% and 77% in April, July and October 2026 (24% for 1 to 6 Nov).
- Any single swap can be checked without an account on 1Click's public status endpoint, for example the largest one: [`/v0/status?depositAddress=0xabe5...Af9b`](https://1click.chaindefuser.com/v0/status?depositAddress=0xabe527cA4C38c6BBd09Ffd583a468223A33bAf9b).
- Source and method, reproducible from public data: the NEAR Intents explorer ([ZEC sold](https://explorer.near-intents.org/?referral=shapeshift&fromTokenId=nep141:zec.omft.near), [ZEC bought](https://explorer.near-intents.org/?referral=shapeshift&toTokenId=nep141:zec.omft.near)), and Midgard's actions endpoint for [Maya (`ssmaya`)](https://midgard.mayachain.info/v2/actions?affiliate=ssmaya&asset=ZEC.ZEC&type=swap&limit=50) and THORChain (`ss`), each priced with the venue's own USD values. DAO fees are what reached the DAO's own accounts; on NEAR Intents the app requests twice the DAO's fee because 1Click keeps half ([`APP_FEE_SPLIT_MULTIPLIER = 2`](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/blob/34854b2509432347dc23ea58e19e4996a21df9ea/packages/swapper/src/swappers/NearIntentsSwapper/constants.ts#L10)), and only the DAO's half is counted here.

**Work packages claimed** (all merged and public):

1. **Ledger.** Every Ledger send was rejected at broadcast. Four causes, documented in [`ZCASH_LEDGER_IMPLEMENTATION.md`](https://github.com/shapeshift/hdwallet/blob/master/ZCASH_LEDGER_IMPLEMENTATION.md) ([hdwallet#765](https://github.com/shapeshift/hdwallet/pull/765)):
   - `splitTransaction` needed the `["zcash","sapling"]` additionals to parse previous transactions;
   - the wrong `isSegwit` flag made the Ledger Zcash app quit over USB;
   - the Ledger library version we had pinned still used the NU6 branch ID after NU6.1 activated, fixed by moving to [`@ledgerhq/hw-app-btc`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ledgerhq/hw-app-btc) 10.13.0;
   - the main one, inside Ledger's own `@ledgerhq/hw-app-btc`: it computes each previous txid with Bitcoin's double SHA-256, while Zcash v5 uses the [ZIP-244](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0244) txid, so the device signed a spend of an input that does not exist. We replaced `getTrustedInputBIP143` for Zcash inputs only and feed it the real txid from our indexer. Every other coin still runs Ledger's code.

   Then:
   - shared UTXO derivation fixed for bs58check v4 ([hdwallet#763](https://github.com/shapeshift/hdwallet/pull/763));
   - Ledger PSBTs moved onto our own bitcoinjs-lib fork, which also fixed back-to-back sends spending unconfirmed change ([hdwallet#768](https://github.com/shapeshift/hdwallet/pull/768), [web#11374](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/11374));
   - Ledger enabled in the app ([web#11337](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/11337));
   - the fix kept working when hdwallet moved into the web monorepo ([commit 5df2c1b0b6](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/commit/5df2c1b0b6));
   - later folded into one pnpm patch of [`hw-app-btc@10.13.0`](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/blob/34854b2509432347dc23ea58e19e4996a21df9ea/patches/@ledgerhq__hw-app-btc@10.13.0.patch) ([web#12638](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12638)).

   [ZCG#81](https://github.com/ZcashCommunityGrants/zcashcommunitygrants/issues/81) said Ledger would only be "considered", and its completion post listed it under "what's next".
2. **Trezor.** Version, version group ID and branch ID passed to Trezor Connect, fixing "incorrect consensus branch id" ([hdwallet#766](https://github.com/shapeshift/hdwallet/pull/766)); Trezor enabled in the app ([web#11338](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/11338)); ZEC hidden on wallets that can't sign it ([web#11307](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/11307), [web#11327](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/11327)).
3. **NEAR Intents and THORChain.** ZEC mapped to NEAR Intents 1Click, live at launch ([web#11298](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/11298)). That mapping is two lines because it sits on our NEAR Intents swapper ([web#11016](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/11016), Nov 2025), so we also price ZEC's share of that swapper by USD volume (15.6%, about half a day). THORChain ZEC swaps first appear in October 2026 (3 Oct in our affiliate data), and our automated asset regeneration picked ZEC up on 5 Oct ([web#12732](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12732)) with no new code, because the adapter and memo path were already there.
4. **Network upgrades.** Every upgrade changes the consensus branch ID that signatures commit to. NU6.2 ([web#12443](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12443)) restored native and Trezor; NU6.3 ([web#12638](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12638)) did the same and found Ledger had been broken since NU6.2, fixed its branch table, and moved the Zcash consensus constants into one shared file. An upgrade still touches that file plus the branch table in our Ledger library patch, and needs a release and a send test on each wallet. NU7 is fixed in [web#12825](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12825), and mainnet sends after the fix went through from native ([2676d2d3…](https://blockchair.com/zcash/transaction/2676d2d3618edace199d145bd998e496b00593381d40cc072e9db1d9ff50ba55)) and Ledger ([771b5388…](https://blockchair.com/zcash/transaction/771b5388fcafeb4ae01b3d5561c77d4dd40df5118f8e60b46393166f3b47fa8a)). Trezor takes the branch ID from the host, so the same fix applies; we have not made a Trezor mainnet send since NU7.
5. **Public API.** ZEC in the API's supported chains ([web#12432](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12432)) and a Zcash adapter wired into the API ([web#12446](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12446)), so third parties quote and execute ZEC swaps with no Zcash infrastructure of their own. Deposit-address swaps tracked from the quote alone ([web#12652](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12652)).
6. **Swap widget and swap-service.** ZEC in the embeddable widget ([web#12435](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12435), [web#12588](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12588), [web#12768](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12768)). Then a deposit-address flow, so anyone can swap by sending funds from any wallet on NEAR Intents and Chainflip routes. The widget cannot sign Zcash transactions, so a ZEC sell inside the widget goes through the deposit flow ([web#12663](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12663)). Most of this code serves every chain, so we price only the Zcash share:
   - quote, QR, amount, countdown and status ([web#12594](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12594));
   - deposit addresses for NEAR Intents and Chainflip, with a longer quote deadline when either leg is on a UTXO chain such as Zcash ([web#12650](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12650));
   - Zcash address validation: t1/t3 accepted, unified addresses refused with a Zcash-specific message ([web#12653](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12653));
   - `zcash:` payment URIs ([web#12651](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12651)) and explorer links for ZEC deposits ([web#12670](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12670));
   - NEAR reports no origin hash for a payment from a shielded pool, so swap-service scans the deposit address's history to find it ([microservices#67](https://github.com/shapeshift/microservices/pull/67)).

   Tested on mainnet: ZEC to ETH paid from Zodl, and ZEC to Base USDC.
7. **Reliability.** A Blockchair fallback when our indexer fails ([web#11346](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/11346), closing [web#11344](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/issues/11344), "Zcash sends failing in all envs"); retries when a new block is not yet indexed, a race production logged on Zcash and Litecoin ([unchained#1308](https://github.com/shapeshift/unchained/pull/1308), priced at the Zcash share).

**Scope intentionally excluded** ([ZCG#81](https://github.com/ZcashCommunityGrants/zcashcommunitygrants/issues/81) milestones and budget lines, listed for context, priced at $0):
- Zcash transaction support in our bitcoinjs-lib fork, [ZIP-243](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0243)/244 ([bitcoinjs-lib#3](https://github.com/shapeshift/bitcoinjs-lib/pull/3)), and built-in wallet signing ([hdwallet#760](https://github.com/shapeshift/hdwallet/pull/760)): milestone 2.
- The Zcash coinstack and its fee endpoint ([unchained#1198](https://github.com/shapeshift/unchained/pull/1198), [unchained#1225](https://github.com/shapeshift/unchained/pull/1225)): milestone 1. Hosting: the $36,000 line.
- The app's chain adapter and production rollout ([web#11290](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/11290), [web#11308](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/11308)): milestone 2.
- Maya, including zcashd RPC for OP_RETURN memos ([web#11299](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/11299), [unchained#1254](https://github.com/shapeshift/unchained/pull/1254)): milestone 3.
- Keeping the node up inside [ZCG#81](https://github.com/ZcashCommunityGrants/zcashcommunitygrants/issues/81)'s hosting year: the NOWNodes migration ([unchained#1267](https://github.com/shapeshift/unchained/pull/1267)) and BIP44 xpub paths ([unchained#1275](https://github.com/shapeshift/unchained/pull/1275)).
- Marketing: the $14,000 line.

### Technical Approach (how you did it)

- **Signing.** Transparent v5 transactions with the [ZIP-244](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0244) sighash and txid (and v4 with [ZIP-243](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0243) for earlier network upgrades), in ShapeShift's bitcoinjs-lib fork, used by the built-in wallet and, since [hdwallet#768](https://github.com/shapeshift/hdwallet/pull/768), for Ledger PSBTs. Branch ID and activation height live in one file, [`packages/hdwallet-core/src/bitcoin.ts`](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/blob/34854b2509432347dc23ea58e19e4996a21df9ea/packages/hdwallet-core/src/bitcoin.ts), shared by native, Ledger and Trezor; the Ledger library patch below carries its own copy of the branch table.
- **Ledger.** Rather than fork Ledger's library for one coin, the Zcash path is one pnpm patch of [`@ledgerhq/hw-app-btc@10.13.0`](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/blob/34854b2509432347dc23ea58e19e4996a21df9ea/patches/@ledgerhq__hw-app-btc@10.13.0.patch): the branch-ID table for each upgrade plus the ZIP-244 trusted-input fix, applied to Zcash inputs only.
- **Fees** (ZCG#81 scope, not priced). [ZIP-317](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0317) fee-aware coin selection (5,000 zat marginal fee, 2 grace actions), counting the OP_RETURN output on memo swaps.
- **Widget and API.** Swaps are quoted and tracked by deposit address, so the user's wallet never connects. When NEAR reports no origin hash (as it does for a payment from a shielded pool), swap-service searches the transparent deposit address's history to find the payment.
- **What we send to swap venues.** In the app, NEAR Intents 1Click quotes are requested from the user's browser, so 1Click sees the user's IP; through the public API and widget, ShapeShift's server makes the request, and the request it builds has no user-IP field. Each request carries the swap parameters, the refund and destination addresses, the `shapeshift` referral, the DAO's fee account and our partner key, and no name, email or account data ([`helpers.ts`](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/blob/4b33d61dc7ed38df47ae23460cd0ae67e96bb0f9/packages/swapper/src/swappers/NearIntentsSwapper/utils/helpers.ts#L200-L249)). NEAR Intents screens those addresses ([its compliance page](https://docs.near-intents.org/security-compliance/risk-and-compliance)), including on price quotes once a wallet is connected. Maya and THORChain quotes go through ShapeShift-hosted nodes, and the only extra data on chain is the standard swap memo.
- **For the next team.** [`ZCASH_LEDGER_IMPLEMENTATION.md`](https://github.com/shapeshift/hdwallet/blob/master/ZCASH_LEDGER_IMPLEMENTATION.md) walks through each Ledger failure and fix, for anyone integrating Zcash through [`@ledgerhq/hw-app-btc`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ledgerhq/hw-app-btc).

### Time Period of Work Completion

7 Nov 2025 to 6 Nov 2026: from the NEAR Intents swapper ([web#11016](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/11016)) to the NU7 fix ([web#12825](https://github.com/shapeshift/web/pull/12825)). ZEC live in production since v1.980.0 (9 Dec 2025).

Rate: ShapeShift DAO's public senior engineer rate, $17,500 per month ([SCP-224](https://snapshot.box/#/s:shapeshiftdao.eth/proposal/0x5138ce866d18844cec8de87b56c22666f3761535efb7f01d654dcd0e9ebfcf7d)), about $101 an hour at 40 hours a week. Line 8 is other people's time on the same PRs: code reading at 500 lines an hour ([SmartBear](https://smartbear.com/learn/code-review/best-practices-for-peer-code-review/)), half an hour per recorded hardware test, and releases cut by someone other than the author. Every PR is linked under Proof of Completion.

Zafe is an open source multisig for shielded ZEC, live on Google Play. Members approve from their phones whenever they want, nobody has to be online at the same time, and the last approval sends the payment.

Groups holding ZEC together usually end up with one person holding the key, or a transparent multisig where everyone can see everything. FROST fixes that, but the tools so far need all signers around at the same time to sign.

Rust core on ZF's FROST crates and librustzcash, a Flutter app, and a small relay that only passes encrypted messages. Anyone can run their own relay. Details are in the [spec](https://github.com/zafe-cash/zafe/blob/main/spec.md).

- [X] I understand all grants are valued in USD but will be disbursed in Shielded ZEC. I acknowledge and accept that disbursement amounts may fluctuate based on the ZEC/USD exchange rate at the time of payment.

### Application Owners (@octocat, @octocat1)

@MeghVyas3132, @Antxnrx

### Organization or Individual Name

Mirage (Megh Vyas and Anton, independent developers)

### Additional Team Members

- **Name:** Anton (@Antxnrx)
- **Role:** Frontend and UI/UX
- **Background:** Frontend engineer and designer. Built Floor (ETHGlobal Mumbai 2026) with Megh.
- **Responsibilities:** Mirage web app, the check / plan / report screens, demo video and visuals.

### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

The Zcash Community Forum, through the Q4 2026 call for proposals.

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

$2,880

### Category

Wallets

### Project Summary

Mirage is a send guard for Zcash wallets: before ZEC leaves the shielded pool, it scores how easy that exit is to link to an earlier entry, sends shielded when it can, and otherwise splits the amount inside the pool and lets the pieces out on a schedule, re-checking each one. The scoring and planning ship as `mirage-core`, a dependency-free npm library any wallet can call.

### Project Description

Inside the shielded pool nothing is visible, but the value and time of every crossing into or out of the pool are public. If an exit amount matches a recent entry, an observer can pair them. Amount-and-timing matching linked 31.5% of coins sent to shielded addresses ([Quesnelle 2017](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.01210)), and Arkham reported labelling over half of ZEC transactions without breaking any cryptography ([crypto.news](https://crypto.news/zcash-privacy-tested-as-arkham-tracks-53percent-of-zec/)). Wallets warn that a send is "public" but do not say whether *this* exit is linkable.

Existing linkability checkers (zcrowd, am-i-linkable, CipherScan's privacy risk detection) run separately, before you send; zcrowd lists the wallet hook as roadmap. Mirage is that hook: the check lives inside the send and acts on the result.

- **Shielded destination:** a fully shielded send with an encrypted memo.
- **Transparent destination** (e.g. an exchange deposit): scored against an index of every public shield and deshield. A crowd of similar crossings → sent. Few or none → held, and a guarded exit is proposed: one fully shielded self-send splits the amount into common denominations inside the pool; each piece then leaves separately on a schedule and is re-checked right before it goes.
- **"Check only"** runs entirely in the browser: the page downloads the public index and scores locally, so the amount never reaches a server.
- **Privacy report card:** every past exit from the wallet, re-scored as it looked at the time (own crossing excluded), 0–100.

**Custody model (clarified after FPF review):** Mirage itself holds no keys and runs no coordinator; it never pools or touches other users' funds. The spending keys live in the wallet engine Mirage drives (zkool_graphql), and that engine signs each scheduled piece automatically when it is due, so the user does not need to be online. Whoever runs the wallet engine therefore holds the keys:
- **Self-hosted** (`docker compose up`, the intended setup): the engine runs on the user's own machine, so the user keeps custody. The machine has to stay online for scheduled pieces to go out.
- **Our hosted testnet demo:** the two demo wallets are held by us, the operators. That is acceptable for testnet TAZ only, and the README says so.

Also disclosed: a piece that still scores red is held and re-checked up to 6 times (2 hours apart), then sent anyway so funds are never stuck (`MAX_HOLDS` in `server/src/jobs.ts`).

Built on 4 Nov 2026 at the Free Society Hackathon (Mumbai, Devcon week, privacy track), then documented and deployed.

### Technical Approach (how you did it)

- **Indexer** (`server/src/indexer.ts`): reads lightwalletd compact blocks (LightWalletD v0.6.1 at testnet.zec.rocks) and classifies every transaction as a shield or deshield across Sapling, Orchard and Ironwood, resolving older transparent inputs on demand.
- **Scoring and planning** (`packages/core`, published as [`mirage-core` 0.1.0](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mirage-core) on 4 Nov 2026): `assess(index, {zats, time})` returns the crowd size and candidate entries; `planExit(zats)` splits into common denominations. No dependencies, 8 tests. Browser and server run the same code; the browser-local check matches the server on 18/18 test amounts against the live index.
- **Guard** (`server/src/api.ts`, `/api/send` and `/api/guarded-exit`) and **scheduler** (`server/src/jobs.ts`): hold linkable sends and re-check each piece before release.
- **Wallet engine:** zkool_graphql v6.36.0 (hhanh00/zkool2) on a private network.
- **Stack:** Node 22, TypeScript 5, Hono 4, @grpc/grpc-js, lightwallet-protocol protos (vendored, MIT), Docker (`docker compose up`).
- **Licence:** MIT. **Contributing guide:** [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/MeghVyas3132/Mirage-Zcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

### Time Period of Work Completion

4 Nov 2026 – 9 Nov 2026

### Total Budget (USD)

$2,880

### Budget Breakdown

**Compensation:** $2,880
**Justification:** Megh Vyas, ~28 h (indexer, `mirage-core` scoring and planning, guard, scheduler, zkool integration, deployment, docs) and Anton, ~20 h (web app, check / plan / report screens, demo video), at $60/h.

**Technology/Software:** $0
**Justification:** Open-source stack only (zkool, lightwalletd, lightwallet-protocol).

**Infrastructure/Hosting:** $0
**Justification:** None claimed (future hosting is not eligible for a retroactive grant; removed after FPF review on 10 Nov 2026).

**Services/Contractors:** $0
**Justification:** None.

**Other:** $0
**Justification:** None.

**Total:** $2,880

### Previous Funding

No

### Previous Funding Details

_No response_

### Other Funding Sources

Yes

### Other Funding Sources Details

Mirage was entered in the Free Society Hackathon privacy track (4 Nov 2026). Results had not been announced as of 10 Nov 2026. **If a prize is awarded before voting opens, we will withdraw this application** so the same work is not paid twice. We may separately apply to Zcash Community Grants for new, forward-looking milestones (a mainnet index and a wallet integration); none of the completed work in this application would be part of that request.

### Success Metrics

- **Shipped:** a live app, a published library (`mirage-core` on npm), and an end-to-end guarded exit on testnet with public txids.
- **Correctness:** browser-local scores match server scores on 18/18 test amounts; `mirage-core` has 8 unit tests.
- **Reuse:** any wallet can call `assess()` / `planExit()` with no dependencies.
- **Wallet-team review:** requested from the zkool maintainer (Mirage is built on zkool_graphql): https://github.com/hhanh00/zkool2/issues/1638. If no wallet maintainer has reviewed it by 13 Nov 2026, we will withdraw and resubmit in a later quarter.

- **Deployment:** https://mirage.140-238-167-7.nip.io (Zcash testnet; pick the `demo-user` wallet)

- **In-pool split, the guarded exit's prepare step (0 public inputs/outputs):** https://testnet.zecblock.com/tx/78644a966fa467cf3aa99d631d004a3f3b9bcb70500a68145fdd21b3607e1cf0
- **Demo video:** https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1jCXO3tLNZINpPmWZkbuI2iZwSORfaUmd?usp=sharing

All completed work will be verified and accepted by its intended users or their representatives, who will confirm that the outputs meet the required quality, functionality, and usability before the work is listed as an option for Coinholder voting.

- [x] I understand when contributing to existing Zcash code, I am required to adhere to the project specific contribution guidelines, paying close attention to any [merge](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#merge-workflow), [branch](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#branch-history), [pull request](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-review), and [commit](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages) guidelines as exemplified in the librustzcash repository.
- [x] I understand all grants are valued in USD but will be disbursed in Shielded ZEC. I acknowledge and accept that disbursement amounts may fluctuate based on the ZEC/USD exchange rate at the time of payment.

### Application Owners (@octocat, @octocat1)

@alvorado-lab

### Organization or Individual Name

Jason Key

### Additional Team Members

```team-members.yaml
None
```

### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

The Zcash Community Forum (Retroactive Grants category).

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

$15,000

### Category

Wallets

### Project Summary

zec_wallet lets any Flutter app send and receive shielded ZEC as an ordinary package dependency, with the keys kept in a Rust core built on librustzcash, and it shipped NU7 support before mainnet activated the upgrade. An optional drop-in wallet UI, native screen protection and Tor come with it, all published on pub.dev and crates.io.

### Project Description

Before this work, a Flutter developer who wanted shielded ZEC in their app had nothing to depend on. The Flutter Zcash wallets that exist are apps, not libraries, so the next team starts from zero (discussed in the [forum thread](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/a-flutter-sdk-for-zcash-ffi-over-librustzcash-with-a-drop-in-shielded-wallet-ui/56639)). zec_wallet closes that gap. A shop app, a messenger or a game can add one dependency and take or send private payments without becoming a wallet team.

What is published, under the verified pub.dev publisher relim.io:

- **zec_wallet**: the SDK. Create or restore a wallet (BIP39), sync over lightwalletd/Zaino, shielded send and receive (Orchard and Sapling), ZIP-321 payment URIs, ZIP-302 memos, ZIP-320 (TEX) two-step sends, an offline send queue, shielding of transparent funds, history, watch-only wallets through UFVK export and import (ZIP-316; asked for in the forum thread and shipped), swaps behind a pluggable provider port (NEAR Intents as the reference), and a C contract through which a host plugs in its own transport. Releases: 0.0.1 and 0.0.2 (8 October), 0.0.4 (23 October, a security release of the TLS stack), 0.0.5 (31 October, NU7) and 0.0.6 (1 November, Android builds on Gradle 9, which Flutter 3.44 sets up for new apps).
- **zec_wallet_ui** (0.0.1, 0.0.3, 0.0.4): a complete wallet UI that mounts under the host's router: onboarding, backup and restore, send, receive, history, shielding and swaps, themed by the host, in 16 languages.
- **zec_wallet_ui_platform** (0.0.1, 0.0.3): native screen protection for that UI (Android FLAG_SECURE, the iOS app-switcher cover and backup exclusion), with no native code in the host app.
- **zec_wallet_tor** (0.0.1, 0.0.3, 0.0.4, 0.0.5): optional Tor. An app that does not add it carries no Tor code.

And on crates.io, **dialer-tor** (0.1.0 on 3 October, 0.1.1 on 8 October, 0.1.3 on 23 October): the Tor client on its own, usable by any Rust app. Since 0.1.1 each Tor client gets a runtime of its own and shuts down within a budget, so switching Tor off really stops it.

NU7 was the largest piece after the first release. 0.0.5 shipped on 31 October, six days before mainnet activated NU7 at block 3,543,405. It builds the new version 6 transactions and follows ZIP 218's limits. It pauses sending in the last 20 blocks before an activation, so no payment is signed for the wrong branch. It reports payments the upgrade cancelled, returns their funds, and counts confirmations for the faster blocks. On 9 November a funded wallet on an Android phone sent itself a payment on NU7's branch; it confirmed within 2 minutes and arrived.

The status is stated plainly in the READMEs: pre-release and not yet externally audited; the Rust core compiles from source, so a Rust toolchain is needed; wallets run on Android, iOS and macOS. One known issue, a light server lowering recorded subtree heights after a rewind, is tracked publicly as [issue #1](https://github.com/alvorado-lab/zec-wallet/issues/1): the server cannot take funds, and until it is fixed the README advises small amounts and a trusted server.

### Technical Approach (how you did it)

- **Audited code used as-is.** The core is Rust over `zcash_client_backend` and `zcash_client_sqlite`, with `sapling-crypto` and `orchard` unchanged, so consensus and proof code is never reimplemented. Dart talks to it through flutter_rust_bridge; Cargokit builds the native library inside `flutter build`.
- **Keys never enter Dart.** Seeds and spending keys stay in Rust; Dart sees addresses, balances, statuses and typed errors with stable codes. CI policy tests enforce the two allowed crossings (the recovery words for backup and restore, and the viewing key for watch-only).
- **Custody.** The seed is sealed with XChaCha20-Poly1305 under a key held by the OS key store (Android Keystore/StrongBox, iOS Secure Enclave); the wallet database is SQLCipher.
- **Transport.** The wallet dials its server through a host-supplied transport or the optional Tor plugin, and the UI reports the real transport state.
- **Network upgrades.** The SDK checks the branch the server reports before it signs, so a build that does not know an upgrade refuses instead of signing transactions the network would reject. Confirmation depth follows NU7's 25-second blocks from the activation height; a few time estimates still assume 75 seconds and can read up to three times too long, as the changelog says.
- **Process.** Spec first, then code; every money-path change reviewed from several angles; guard tests checked against deliberately planted bugs; money paths proven on mainnet with real ZEC on Android and iOS devices before release; advisories checked against a freshly fetched RustSec database before each publish.

### Time Period of Work Completion

June 2026 to November 2026

### Total Budget (USD)

$15,000

### Budget Breakdown

- Compensation:
  - $(USD): 15,000
  - Justification: My own time: 94 days of commits to the SDK between 12 June and 9 November 2026, requested at about $160 per day, well below a market rate.
- Technology/Software:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: Not claimed.
- Infrastructure/Hosting:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: None.
- Services/Contractors:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: None.
- Other:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: None.
- Total $(USD): 15,000

### Previous Funding

No

### Previous Funding Details

_No response_

### Other Funding Sources

Yes

### Other Funding Sources Details

A Zcash Community Grants application is planned for FORWARD work only: an external security review, prebuilt native binaries, a clean-room reference integration and a maintenance period. This retroactive request covers only the completed, published work above; the two do not overlap.

### Success Metrics

- Four packages live on pub.dev and the Tor client on crates.io, all from one public repository. pub.dev scores them 140 to 160 of 160 points and counts about 3,300 downloads of the four in the last 30 days (my own release checks are part of that count).
- The public CI is green on the current release; on the 0.0.6 release commit it ran 2,622 Rust tests and 2,420 Dart tests.
- NU7 support was on pub.dev six days before NU7 activated; after the activation, a mainnet payment made with it confirmed within 2 minutes.
- Mainnet proof with real ZEC on Android and iOS: shielded sends including ZIP-320 two-step sends, a force-kill in the middle of a send that recovered to exactly one transaction pair on chain, the offline queue, a recovery sweep of funds sent to already-used ephemeral addresses, and an in-place upgrade of a funded wallet from 0.0.4 to 0.0.5 that kept its balance and history. Total losses: transaction fees.
- Two consumers today: the Relim messenger it grew out of, whose tester builds run on 0.0.5 and 0.0.6, and the reference example app. The Relim app also adopted dialer-tor 0.1.1 independently: its probe counted 0 Tor connection attempts after switching Tor off, against 6 to 16 without the fix.
- Built in the open with the community: watch-only support was requested in the forum thread and shipped in the first release.

### Proof of completion

- Repository/Commit:
  - [alvorado-lab/zec-wallet](https://github.com/alvorado-lab/zec-wallet) - the full source, MIT, with CONTRIBUTING.md
- Publication:
  - [zec_wallet](https://pub.dev/packages/zec_wallet), [zec_wallet_ui](https://pub.dev/packages/zec_wallet_ui), [zec_wallet_ui_platform](https://pub.dev/packages/zec_wallet_ui_platform) and [zec_wallet_tor](https://pub.dev/packages/zec_wallet_tor) - on pub.dev under the publisher relim.io
  - [dialer-tor](https://crates.io/crates/dialer-tor) - on crates.io
- Deployment/Release:
  - [Public CI on 0.0.6](https://github.com/alvorado-lab/zec-wallet/actions/runs/41321801631) - green on the release commit
  - [zec_wallet changelog](https://pub.dev/packages/zec_wallet/changelog) - every release, including NU7 in 0.0.5
- Other Evidence:
  - [Forum thread](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/a-flutter-sdk-for-zcash-ffi-over-librustzcash-with-a-drop-in-shielded-wallet-ui/56639) - design discussion and the watch-only request
  - [Issue #1](https://github.com/alvorado-lab/zec-wallet/issues/1) - the one known limitation, disclosed publicly

### Conflict of Interest Disclosure

I also build the Relim messenger, which uses this SDK, and I publish the packages under the relim.io publisher. The grant would fund completed open-source work that any app can use; it does not fund Relim.

I understand this is required in order for the community to discuss and vote on this grant application. issues.body:
### Terms and Conditions

- [x] I agree to the [Grant Agreement](https://9ba4718c-5c73-47c3-a024-4fc4e5278803.usrfiles.com/ugd/9ba471_6ff6db4095fd4c4ba21babec361e927e.pdf) terms if funded
