- [x] I agree to disclose conflicts of interest
- [x] I understand that this grant program is only eligible for completed work, as it is a retroactive grant program. Applications for planned or partially completed work will not be considered. All completed work will be verified and accepted by its intended users or their representatives, who will confirm that the outputs meet the required quality, functionality, and usability before the work is listed as an option for Coinholder voting.
- [x] I agree that for any new open-source software, I will create a CONTRIBUTING.md file that reflects the high standards of Zcash development, using the [`librustzcash` style guides](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#styleguides) as a primary reference.
- [x] I understand when contributing to existing Zcash code, I am required to adhere to the project specific contribution guidelines, paying close attention to any [merge](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#merge-workflow), [branch](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#branch-history), [pull request](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-review), and [commit](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages) guidelines as exemplified in the librustzcash repository.
- [x] I understand all grants are valued in USD but will be disbursed in Shielded ZEC. I acknowledge and accept that disbursement amounts may fluctuate based on the ZEC/USD exchange rate at the time of payment.

### Application Owners (@octocat, @octocat1)

@0xOucan

### Organization or Individual Name

0xOucan (individual), LeekWallet

### Additional Team Members

```team-members.yaml
- Name: 0xOucan
  Role: Founder and CTO
  Background: Fiscal and financial engineer. Nine years in crypto conferences, community and project management; now building software with AI agents. 17 hackathon wins.
  Responsibilities: Development and communications
```

### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

The Q4 2026 call for proposals on the Zcash Community Forum, and conversations at ZCon7.

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

$6,770

### Category

Wallets

### Project Summary

LeekWallet Zcash is an open-source DIY hardware wallet for Zcash, built from about $25 of generic parts (ESP32-S3), that verifies and signs shielded transactions as a PCZT signer (ZIP 374) and shows the user what it signs. It ships with a Zodl fork that adds hardware signing, a desktop and Android wallet, a Chrome extension, a CLI and a browser simulator, all released with signed checksums. Since then: an integration SDK (Rust, with Kotlin and Swift bindings) so other wallets can add the board, a public docs site, and a pre-ZIP for per-app storage keys derived by the signer.

### Project Description

**The problem.** Holding shielded ZEC on a hardware device today means trusting a closed device or the computer you sign from. Few hardware signers support Orchard, and there was no open, cheap device that anyone can build, read end to end and verify.

**What was built (completed and public):**

- **Board firmware** (ESP32-S3, 128×128 OLED, rotary knob, one Cancel button). It holds the seed (BIP39, ZIP 32, unified addresses).
  - Signs **Ironwood (NU6.3) and Orchard spends and transparent P2PKH inputs** (shielding), with memos.
  - Works as a **PCZT signer**: it parses the PCZT, checks that the spends belong to its keys, recomputes the sighash, rebuilds the note and value commitments and the memo ciphertext, shows the outputs and memo, and returns only RedPallas spend-auth signatures (~110 B), bound to the SHA-256 of the exact bytes it reviewed.
  - Signs from a **compact PCZT view** (~1.4 KB instead of ~2.8 KB).
  - **Address verification:** it proves a displayed address, including a rotated diversified one, is its own (Orchard `pk_d = [ivk]·g_d`, index recovered by FF1), and refuses foreign or mixed addresses.
  - **Network guard:** the board is set to mainnet or testnet and refuses requests for the other network.
  - **Links:** USB serial, Bluetooth LE (an encrypted session: X25519, HKDF, ChaCha20-Poly1305, with a six-digit passkey), and SD card for air-gapped use.
  - **Two independent signers**, C on the device and Rust on the host, cross-checked against shared test vectors generated from librustzcash.
- **Zodl fork** (MIT, two apps: mainnet and testnet). A hardware-signer account whose keys stay on the board, signed over USB or Bluetooth, with "Verify on device". Release 3.17.0-leek.2.
- **Zcash LeekWallet app** (Tauri 2: Linux, Windows, macOS, Android). A full light wallet:
  - syncs, sends and shields with signatures from the board;
  - supports watch-only wallets;
  - swaps ZEC through NEAR Intents.
- **Chrome extension:** librustzcash in WebAssembly, the wallet stored in OPFS, the board over Web Serial and Web Bluetooth.
- **`zecz` CLI and Rust libraries** (`zecz-core`, `leek-device`, `leek-android`) that all the companions share.
- **Board simulator and test vectors:** the firmware's own protocol and signers on a PTY for hardware-free testing. Keys and PCZTs, both valid and refused, generated from librustzcash.
- **Website** with a simulated board you can wire, unlock and sign with in the browser, verify-first downloads, and a web flasher.
- **Release v0.1.0 "Sacbeh":**
  - firmware (reproducible build), desktop bundles, Android APK and Chrome extension;
  - a `SHA256SUMS` signed with SSH, plus signed git tags.
- **Real transactions** signed on the board: testnet over USB, Bluetooth and SD, and the first mainnet sends, a shield, and a ZEC → USDC swap through NEAR Intents.
- **Integration SDK (after the hackathon, 2026-10-31 to 2026-11-03).** Motivated by conversations with the Zodl, Zingo and Zillions teams: one SDK instead of a separate integration per wallet.
  - `leek-zcash` (Rust): preflight, the signer view, `sign_pczt`, `apply_zsig` (every signature verified before it is applied), persisting the signed result and txid before broadcast, a check that the mined transaction is the one signed, typed errors with stable codes.
  - `leek-zcash-ffi`: UniFFI bindings for Kotlin (Android) and Swift (iOS); the app owns the USB / Bluetooth transport; progress and cancel.
- **Privacy and safety on the board (same period):**
  - the board asks "Share view key?" before releasing the UFVK; a fingerprint-only call identifies the board without it;
  - the six-digit pairing code is required on every connection (no remembered hosts);
  - an encrypted request is never answered in plaintext, even when the session ends mid-request;
  - transactions with duplicate action keys (`rk`) are refused;
  - an audit of the SD-card and flash writes, with power cuts simulated after every write; two high findings fixed (an unreadable vault no longer treated as empty; a crash-safe PIN key migration).
- **Pre-ZIP "Hardware-Wallet App Storage Keys":** the signer derives a per-app key (ZIP 32 Registered key derivation) so a light wallet can keep its UFVK and database encrypted, released only after an OK on the board; implemented in the firmware and the SDK, with test vectors. [Draft](https://zcash.leekwallet.xyz/docs/reference/protocol/zip-draft-app-storage-keys/).
- **Docs site:** https://zcash.leekwallet.xyz/docs, live: getting started, security and limits, an integration guide, the simulator, and a reference imported from the repositories (firmware, protocol, audits, SDK), with offline search.
- **Outreach:** a demo video, a website walkthrough, showing the board in person at ZCon7, and forum write-ups (security discussion on supply chain and side channels, and a [project update](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/leekwallet-zcash-update-an-sdk-for-wallet-integrations-docs-a-colour-screen-build-and-a-pre-zip/58857)). Videos: [docs tour](https://youtu.be/bPQU5pULTPE), [SDK integration](https://youtu.be/9JXgmRCI91w), [pre-ZIP in 60 seconds](https://youtu.be/F-YRyLxuLzI).

**Not claimed here:** work after November 3 is not part of this application. That includes the NU7 update (on `main`, not yet released or tested on a board), the colour screen kit and the OPTIGA Trust M bring-up, which are still in progress.

**Status, stated honestly:**
- The project is experimental and not audited.
- Flash encryption and secure boot are deliberately off (no eFuses burned), so physical access to the board can read its flash. This is documented in the README, with the stateless and SD-card modes as mitigations.

### Technical Approach (how you did it)

- **Starting point (not billed here):** my own earlier open-source ESP32 hardware wallet, LeekWallet. The tag `pre-zecathon` (2026-09-23) marks it. From it I reused the screen, buttons, PIN, encrypted vault and the USB/Bluetooth transport. Its EVM code was removed; everything listed above for Zcash was written from 2026-10-14 (`git diff pre-zecathon..main`: 355 commits in the main repository, 48 in the Zodl fork).
- **Firmware:** ESP-IDF 5.5 through PlatformIO. The Zcash code is in `firmware/src/zcash-*.c`, a C signer in `components/zsign-c`, and a Rust signer in `components/zsign-rust`. Host-side unit tests build the firmware's C code for Linux.
- **Host:** Rust on librustzcash for keys, sync (lightwalletd), PCZT construction (ZIP 374), proving and the wallet database. `leek-device` defines the device client and the `.zsig` format. `leek-android` is the JNI library loaded by the Zodl fork.
- **Apps:**
  - Tauri 2 for desktop and Android;
  - Kotlin modules in the Zodl fork;
  - an MV3 Chrome extension with a Rust → WebAssembly engine.
- **Verification and release:**

- [x] I understand all grants are valued in USD but will be disbursed in Shielded ZEC. I acknowledge and accept that disbursement amounts may fluctuate based on the ZEC/USD exchange rate at the time of payment.

### Application Owners (@octocat, @octocat1)

@JayWebtech

### Organization or Individual Name

Jethro Adamu

### Additional Team Members

```team-members.yaml
None
```

### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

Twitter

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

10500

### Category

Non-Wallet Applications

### Project Summary

PetraPay is a non-custodial, Stripe-style payment gateway: customers pay with 190+ tokens on any chain, and businesses receive shielded ZEC at a fresh Orchard address, online through invoices, payment links and a developer API, and in person through an Android point-of-sale app with printed receipts.

### Project Description

Most people who could pay a Zcash merchant don't hold ZEC. They hold USDC, ETH, SOL or BTC. That forces merchants who want Zcash-level privacy to either turn those customers away or settle to a transparent wallet. PetraPay removes that trade-off: the customer pays with whatever they hold, and the merchant receives shielded ZEC.

**What it does (online and in person):**
- Invoices and reusable payment links (fixed price or customer-chooses) with optional custom checkout fields. Links can be edited at any time without changing their URL.
- Customers pay with 190+ tokens on any supported chain via a connected wallet (EVM/Solana) or QR, after seeing a signed quote with fees included. They can also pay shielded ZEC directly via a ZIP-321 QR.
- Exact settlement: the merchant receives the exact invoiced ZEC amount at an Orchard address.
- Built-in off-ramp: merchants can withdraw ZEC to any token on any supported chain.
- Drop-in checkout for any website: the open-source `petrapay` npm package adds a "Pay with PetraPay" button (React component, web component or plain JS) that opens the hosted checkout in a popup and notifies the site when the customer has paid. No API key in the browser.
- Developer API for stores: secret API keys, a REST API to create checkouts (order reference, metadata, redirect URLs, expiry), idempotency keys, and HMAC-signed webhooks with automatic retries and a delivery log.
- Full documentation site: guides, API reference, SDK, webhook verification samples, testing and self-hosting.
- Non-custodial and self-hostable: PetraPay never holds funds or keys.

**Point of sale (in-person payments):**
- A native Android POS app for payment terminals with a built-in 58 mm thermal printer (tested on the Senraise H10), and other Android devices.
- The cashier enters an amount in USD or ZEC; the terminal shows a QR with a 15-minute timer. The customer scans it with their phone and pays with any supported token or shielded ZEC.
- When the payment lands, the terminal shows "Paid" and prints a receipt automatically, with a QR linking to the online receipt.
- Terminals pair with a one-time, 10-minute code. A terminal can only create and view its own sales and can be revoked instantly.

**How it complements existing Zcash payment tools:** processors like CipherPay serve customers who already hold ZEC and detect payments via the merchant's viewing key. PetraPay targets the far larger group who don't hold ZEC, converting their payments into shielded ZEC, online and at a physical counter. It never asks for a viewing key, and every PetraPay payment converts non-Zcash money into shielded ZEC.

**Privacy model:**
- Funds settle into the Orchard pool.
- Each payment uses a fresh unified address from a pool the merchant supplies (e.g. from Zashi)
- ZIP-316 parsing (validated against the official test vectors) rejects transparent and Sapling-only addresses; an Orchard receiver is required.
- No email or password: accounts are ed25519 keys derived from a 12-word phrase that never leaves the browser.

### Technical Approach (how you did it)

Architecture: TypeScript monorepo (pnpm), about 31,000 lines of code.
- Web: Next.js (App Router), Tailwind; deployed on Vercel at petrapay.xyz.
- API: Node.js + Fastify, PostgreSQL via Prisma, background worker; deployed on Railway at api.petrapay.xyz.
- Shared package: Zcash utilities and API schemas (zod).
- POS: React Native Android app with Kotlin native modules.
- SDK: `petrapay` on npm (ESM, CJS and a script-tag build), with React bindings.

**Cross-chain routing:** NEAR Intents 1Click API (official SDK). Customer payments are EXACT_OUTPUT quotes so the merchant receives an exact ZEC amount; withdrawals are EXACT_INPUT. Every quote's signature is verified (verifyQuoteSignature), and the echoed recipient, assets and refund address must match the request before a deposit address is shown. Memo-based deposit mode is used automatically for chains that need it (e.g. Stellar). A worker polls swap status and moves checkouts OPEN → PROCESSING → PAID. Refunds go to the payer's own address.

**Zcash specifics:**
- ZIP-316 unified address decoding (bech32m + F4Jumble) implemented and tested against the official test vectors; Orchard receiver required.
- ZIP-321 payment URIs for direct shielded payments.
- Per-payment address pool assigned with SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so concurrent checkouts never share an address.
- Verified against the live API that Orchard-only unified addresses are accepted as ZEC recipients.

**Accounts and encryption:** ed25519 identity derived from a BIP-39 phrase and held as a non-extractable WebCrypto key; challenge-response login. Checkout form answers are sealed with X25519 ECDH + HKDF-SHA256 + AES-GCM in the customer's browser.

**Merchant API:** SHA-256-hashed secret keys (pp_sk_), Stripe-style /v1 REST API, idempotency records (24h), per-key rate limiting, transactional webhook outbox with HMAC-SHA256 signatures, exponential backoff retries over ~2 days, and SSRF protection on webhook URLs.

**Checkout SDK:** the hosted checkout opens in a popup (so browser wallets work, and checkout pages keep X-Frame-Options: DENY). The checkout page posts payment.created / processing / paid events to the opening window; the SDK accepts them only from the popup it opened and from the PetraPay origin. Pay-what-you-want links accept a pre-filled amount, so a store can pass its cart total. Tested end to end in headless Chrome.

**Point of sale:**
- Printer: native module binding the terminal's built-in printer service (AIDL) for 58 mm receipts with text, QR and layout.
- Secure storage: terminal credentials kept in Android Keystore-backed encrypted storage.
- Pairing: one-time pairing codes (hashed, 10-minute expiry) exchanged for a scoped terminal token.
- Sales are normal checkouts (source: "pos"), reusing the same quote verification, address pool, settlement worker and webhooks as online payments.

**Testing**: 44 automated API tests (ZIP-316 vectors, auth, address pool, settlement state machine, payment links and editing, merchant API, webhook signing and retries, POS pairing and test mode) plus SDK unit tests.

**Timeline**: initial build late September 2026; payment links and encrypted forms early October; invoice editing, deployment and the merchant API/webhooks through October; POS app, test mode, documentation site, the npm SDK, link editing and the five merchant integrations in early November 2026.

### Time Period of Work Completion

September 2026 – October 2026

### Total Budget (USD)

10500

### Budget Breakdown

- Compensation:
  - $(USD): $10,500
  - Justification: 300 hours of solo design, development, testing and deployment at $35/hr, from Sep 29 to Nov 9, 2026 (about 6 weeks). Hours by workstream, each verifiable in the repository:
    • Payments core and Zcash, 70 h: ZIP-316 unified address decoding (bech32m + F4Jumble) tested against the official vectors; Orchard-only validation; per-payment shielded address pool with row locking; signed-quote verification and request matching; settlement worker (OPEN → PROCESSING → PAID, refunds); ZIP-321 direct-pay URIs.
    • Web app and hosted checkout, 80 h: merchant dashboard; invoices with editing; payment links (fixed or customer-chooses, editable, with form answers encrypted in the browser via X25519 + AES-GCM); hosted checkout for 190+ tokens with wallet connect and live quotes; withdrawals (ZEC to any token); recovery-phrase accounts.
    • Merchant API and webhooks, 40 h: pp_sk_ secret keys (hashed at rest), Stripe-style /v1 REST API, idempotency keys, rate limiting, HMAC-signed webhooks with retries and a delivery log, SSRF protection, and the 44-test automated suite.
    • Android POS app, 45 h: React Native app with Kotlin native modules for the terminal's built-in printer (58 mm receipts with QR) and Keystore-backed storage; one-time terminal pairing with scoped access; per-terminal test mode enforced server-side.
    • npm SDK and documentation, 30 h: the `petrapay` package (React, web component and script-tag builds) with popup checkout and payment events, tested end to end in headless Chrome; an 18-page documentation site with API reference and code samples.
    • Deployment, security and integrations, 35 h: production deployment (Vercel + Railway, custom domains); security hardening (CSP/frame protection, input validation, rate limits); integrating PetraPay into five live merchant sites alongside their existing payment methods.
    $35/hr is below the typical market rate for full-stack developers with blockchain experience; it reflects the value of the delivered work rather than a premium rate.

- Total $(USD): $10,500

### Previous Funding

No

### Previous Funding Details

_No response_

### Other Funding Sources

No

### Other Funding Sources Details

_No response_

### Success Metrics

- **Shipped and live:** a working, deployed product, not a prototype. It includes invoices, payment links, cross-chain checkout, withdrawals, a merchant API with webhooks, an npm checkout SDK, documentation, and an Android point-of-sale app running on real payment hardware.
  • **App:** https://www.petrapay.xyz
  • **Documentation:** https://www.petrapay.xyz/docs
  • **npm package:** https://www.npmjs.com/package/petrapay

- Live with five merchant sites in different industries. Each one added PetraPay next to its existing payment methods with a few lines of code, using the npm package:
  • Keri's Premier (food products store): https://buy.kerispremier.shop/
  • Poultrix (poultry farm management SaaS): https://shop.poultrix.org/
  • Human Stock (people-investing app): https://stock.tryhumanstock.xyz
  • Tetra (bounty platform): https://bounty.trytetra.xyz
  • YTech Engineering (solar and engineering equipment store): https://www.crypto.ytechengineering.com/

- Expands who can pay Zcash merchants: anyone holding one of 190+ tokens on a supported chain can now pay a business and have it settle in shielded ZEC.

- Brings shielded ZEC into physical retail: a shop can accept any token from a walk-in customer and settle to the Orchard pool, with a printed receipt, and neither side needs to run Zcash infrastructure.

- Increases shielded adoption: every payment settles into the Orchard pool at a fresh address, so payments can't be linked on-chain.

- Easy for developers to adopt: a site can add PetraPay with one npm install and a few lines of code (React, web component or plain script tag), with no API key in the browser. Stores that need more can use the documented REST API and signed webhooks.

- Reusable for the ecosystem: open-source and self-hostable, with a documented ZIP-316 implementation, a Stripe-style API and a public npm package other Zcash projects can build on.

### Proof of completion

**Repository:** https://github.com/JayWebtech/petrapay (Sep 29 – Nov 9, 2026; MIT license)

  - Android POS app: apps/pos
  - Checkout SDK: packages/petrapay-js

**npm package:** https://www.npmjs.com/package/petrapay
**POS demo:** https://vimeo.com/1245082077
**POS APK:** https://github.com/JayWebtech/petrapay/raw/main/apk/petrapay-pos-v1.0.apk
**Demo video:** https://vimeo.com/1245079217

**Live merchants (PetraPay offered alongside each site's existing payment methods):**
  - YTech Engineering (equipment store): https://www.crypto.ytechengineering.com/

**Mainnet transactions:**
  - Online payment (e.g. USDC on Solana → shielded ZEC): https://www.petrapay.xyz/pay/6sXvLQrBeN8y

All completed work will be verified and accepted by its intended users or their representatives, who will confirm that the outputs meet the required quality, functionality, and usability before the work is listed as an option for Coinholder voting.

- [x] I understand when contributing to existing Zcash code, I am required to adhere to the project specific contribution guidelines, paying close attention to any [merge](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#merge-workflow), [branch](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#branch-history), [pull request](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-review), and [commit](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages) guidelines as exemplified in the librustzcash repository.
- [x] I understand all grants are valued in USD but will be disbursed in Shielded ZEC. I acknowledge and accept that disbursement amounts may fluctuate based on the ZEC/USD exchange rate at the time of payment.
### Application Owners
 
@mnm458
 
### Organization or Individual Name
 
Mohak Malhotra
 
### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?
 
By being part of the Zcash community
 
### Requested Grant Amount (USD)
 
$47,200
 
### Category
 
Infrastructure
 
### Project Summary
 
Thirteen merged pull requests to Zallet, integration-tests and lightwalletd (March to November 2026), led by four bug fixes. The largest is a fix for a connection-pool deadlock (zcash/zallet#708, fixed in zcash/zallet#914) that could freeze 14 wallet RPCs under load or on small machines, including `z_getnewaccount` on a fresh wallet. The rest add a backup command for live wallets, owner-only file protection on Unix and Windows, zcashd-compatible viewing key RPCs and cookie authentication. All of it is merged and reviewed by Zallet's maintainers.
 
### Project Description
 
Since March 2026 I have contributed 13 merged pull requests to Zallet, Zcash's replacement for the zcashd wallet, and to its test and light-client infrastructure. The work focused on fixing bugs that broke wallets in production and on closing gaps that block zcashd users from migrating.
 
#### Bug fixes
 
1. **Wallet RPC deadlock (zcash/zallet#708, fixed in zcash/zallet#914).** Wallet sync permanently holds 4 pooled database connections. Fourteen wallet RPCs held one connection while acquiring another, so under load or on small machines they could wait forever and block every other RPC. On a fresh wallet it was a bootstrapping deadlock: `z_getnewaccount`, the call that lets sync start, was itself affected. I hit it while running backup end-to-end tests on a small machine and root-caused it with stack samples.
2. **`z_listunspent` failing on one bad memo (zcash/zallet#866).** One unreadable memo, such as a text memo with invalid UTF-8, made the whole call fail and hid every spendable note. Unfetched memos also returned placeholder text in a field documented as hex.
3. **Infinite loop in lightwalletd darkside mode (zcash/lightwalletd#553).** `setPrevhash` computed the block hash before updating the previous-hash bytes, so the loop never ended. Wallet teams use darkside mode to test reorg handling.
4. **Wrong zcashd migration table (zcash/zallet#885).** The Zallet book listed implemented RPCs as missing and gave outdated advice for `sendmany` and `sendtoaddress`. Exchanges use this table to plan their move off zcashd.
#### Wallet safety
 
- **`zallet backup` (zcash/zallet#906):** consistent, integrity-checked backups of a live wallet. A Zallet maintainer suggested I take on zcash/zallet#195 and asked for the live-wallet design.
- **Owner-only file protection (zcash/zallet#913, zcash/zallet#936):** completes maintainer-filed issue zcash/zallet#910. Backup, the RPC cookie, the encryption identity, the data directory and the wallet database now share one permission module across Unix and Windows. On Windows the wallet database previously had no owner-only protection.
#### zcashd parity
 
- `z_importviewingkey` (zcash/zallet#431) and `z_exportviewingkey` (zcash/zallet#614) for Sapling, matching zcashd's interface, plus an integration test (zcash/integration-tests#181)
- RPC cookie authentication (zcash/zallet#502), as in zcashd and bitcoind
- `blockstomaturity` in `z_listunspent` (zcash/zallet#789), used by mining pools
- A shared account-birthday helper for `z_getnewaccount` and `z_recoveraccounts` (zcash/zallet#760)
### Technical Approach (how you did it)
 
All work was done in the upstream repositories ([zcash/zallet](https://github.com/zcash/zallet), [zcash/integration-tests](https://github.com/zcash/integration-tests), [zcash/lightwalletd](https://github.com/zcash/lightwalletd)) and reviewed by their maintainers. For the larger items I agreed the design with a maintainer before building.
 
**Deadlock (zcash/zallet#914).** Root-caused from stack samples on a small machine. Fourteen RPCs now stage their database reads, release the connection before keystore access, and reacquire only once key material is in hand. A new `clippy.toml` bans holding a pooled connection across an `await`, so the bug class fails CI if it returns. The pool now has a floor of 8 connections (4 for sync plus 4 matching zcashd's default RPC threads), because deadpool's default of twice the CPU count is below what sync alone holds on a single-core host. Nine methods that only need network parameters no longer take a connection at all. Verified with an A/B run on a 2-core host.
 
**Unreadable memos (zcash/zallet#866).** Memo lookup returns an explicit outcome (read, not yet fetched, or unreadable). An unreadable memo omits the memo fields for that note and logs a warning identifying it, instead of failing the request.
 
**Backup (zcash/zallet#906).** Uses SQLite's Online Backup API, which gives a transaction-consistent snapshot of a running wallet without blocking it. It fails loudly instead of looping forever if sustained writes keep restarting the copy. It never produces a partial backup: if an unclean shutdown leaves a hot journal, it asks you to start the wallet once to recover first. I agreed that trade-off with a maintainer.
 
**File protection (zcash/zallet#913, zcash/zallet#936).** A single module provides owner-only file creation (mode 0600 forced on Unix regardless of umask, protected ACLs on Windows) and atomic publishing in three explicit modes. No-clobber publishing uses `RENAME_NOREPLACE` via rustix on Linux and macOS (already in the dependency tree, so no new crate) and `MoveFileExW` on Windows. Verified on macOS and Linux, and via a Windows cross-compile.
 
**zcashd parity (zcash/zallet#431, zcash/zallet#614, zcash/zallet#502, zcash/zallet#789).** Matched zcashd's RPC interfaces, including the `whenkeyisnew`/`yes`/`no` rescan options for viewing key import. Cookie auth writes `{datadir}/.cookie` on startup and removes it on clean shutdown, and `zallet rpc` reads it automatically.
 
**lightwalletd (zcash/lightwalletd#553) and docs (zcash/zallet#885).** Fixed the hash ordering in `setPrevhash` and added an 83-line regression test. Corrected the RPC status table and added a test that fails on a mistyped status or a missing row.

### Budget Breakdown

  - $(USD): 45,000
  - Justification: 300 hours at $150/hour. Hours are based on the scope of each PR, including design discussion, review rounds and rebases:

| zcash/zallet#502 | Cookie auth and docs | 22 | 3,300 |

| zcash/zallet#885 | RPC status table fix and drift test | 11 | 1,650 |
| zcash/integration-tests#181 | `z_importviewingkey` integration test | 11 | 1,650 |
| zcash/lightwalletd#553 | Darkside infinite-loop fix and regression test | 8 | 1,200 |
| zcash/zallet#789 | `blockstomaturity` | 7 | 1,050 |
| zcash/zallet#760 | Birthday helper refactor | 5 | 750 |
| **Total** | | **300** | **45,000** |

- Technology/Software: $0
- Infrastructure/Hosting:
  - $(USD): 2,200
  - Justification: Two AWS t2.large hosts (2 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 400 GB storage) running infra, full nodes and Zallet continuously since March 2026, used for development, end-to-end testing and bug reproduction (about 8 months of compute, storage and data transfer).

### Success Metrics
 
Zallet has to be safe and reliable before exchanges, mining pools and custodians can leave zcashd. This work removed real failures in that path, and all of it is merged into the official repositories.
 
- **Bugs fixed:** 4 production bugs, each with a test or lint that prevents it from returning.
- **Deadlock removed from 14 wallet RPCs,** including the one a fresh wallet needs to start syncing. 9 more methods no longer take a database connection at all.
- **Tracked issues closed or completed:** zcash/zallet#708 (deadlock), zcash/zallet#80 (viewing key import), zcash/zallet#305 (cookie auth), zcash/zallet#910 (file permissions, all steps), the manual-backup part of zcash/zallet#195, and zcash/lightwalletd#552.

### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

Through the Zcash Community Forums and the Financial Privacy Foundation's GitHub repository.

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

200

### Category

Non-Wallet Applications

### Project Summary

zcash-donation-widget is an open-source, zero-backend browser widget and payment-link builder that lets any creator accept shielded Zcash testnet donations through ZIP-321 payment links, with memo-based payment confirmation that uses only a viewing key  no server, no account, and no custody of funds.


### Project Description

About me: I am Veevaa Bajaj, an independent creator and final-year design student based in New Delhi, India, building open-source tools for the Zcash testnet ecosystem.

Creators who want to accept ZEC donations today have to run payment infrastructure, use a point-of-sale system, or ask donors to copy raw addresses with no confirmation that a payment arrived. On testnet, where most experimentation happens, there was no small, embeddable, donations-focused package at all.

zcash-donation-widget fills that gap. It is a TypeScript package (MIT licensed) that provides:

- An embeddable donation widget: one function call renders a donation box with amount and message fields on any web page.
- ZIP-321 payment links: shareable links and payment URIs built with the published @z-labs/zip321 library, so any ZIP-321 compatible wallet can pay.
- Strict address validation: ZIP-316 unified addresses and viewing keys are checksum-verified; mainnet addresses are rejected in testnet mode, and spending keys are refused by design.
- Memo-based receipts: the receipt watcher matches an incoming payment by memo and amount using only a Unified Full Viewing Key, so a creator can show a donor "Paid" without a server and without ever holding spending keys.
- A static demo page showing the full flow end to end.

The package has a single runtime dependency (@z-labs/zip321), ships with 26 automated tests (all passing), full TypeScript types, a README with integration instructions, and a CONTRIBUTING.md following Zcash development norms.

Disclosure: receipt watching is implemented against the published lightwalletd client interface and the watch API pattern of the open source zcash-testnet-wallet project. This application claims only the widget, the payment-link builder, the validation layer, and the demo  not the underlying watcher or wallet work, which belongs to its authors.


### Technical Approach (how you did it)

Architecture: a single TypeScript package (ESM, strict mode) with five small modules.

- validate.ts: ZIP-316 unified address and UFVK validation using bech32m decoding and checksum verification. Testnet human-readable prefixes (utest1 / uviewtest1) are accepted; mainnet addresses and spending-key-shaped inputs are rejected.
- link.ts: ZIP-321 payment link builder and parser, built on the published @z-labs/zip321 library (v0.1.1, the package's only runtime dependency). Amounts are handled internally as zatoshis in bigint, never floating point.
- memo.ts: memo encoding within the 512-byte Zcash memo limit, carried in links as base64url without padding.
- widget.ts: the embeddable donation widget. One function call mounts the donation box; a creator configures a single unified address (reused for every donation) or a list of addresses (rotated per donation).
- receipt.ts: a payment watcher that matches an incoming transaction by memo and amount using only a Unified Full Viewing Key, over an injectable lightwalletd client interface (public testnet endpoint testnet.zec.rocks:443), with a configurable timeout that resolves as "expired" when no matching payment arrives.

Process: implemented module by module with tests written against each behaviour (Vitest, 26 tests, all passing), type-checked with tsc, and released as v0.1.0 in November 2026 with a static demo page (demo/index.html) that runs entirely in the browser with no backend.


### Time Period of Work Completion

The work is complete and public. The package is released on GitHub under the MIT license with a working demo page in the repository, full TypeScript types, and 26 automated tests covering address validation, ZIP-321 link building and parsing, memo handling, and receipt matching , including the acceptance case of a 0.01 TAZ donation with a memo round-tripping through the ZIP-321 URI exactly. It is, to my knowledge, the first donations-focused (rather than checkout or point-of-sale) testnet widget package in the Zcash ecosystem, and it is designed so any creator or community site can embed it without running a server.

Core Blockchain Backend Engineer at Reef Chain, Jan 2023 – Jun 2026 — 3 years on a live L1: Reefscan explorer and indexers, Reef SDK (@reef-chain/util-lib, react-lib), create-reef-app, rebuilt Chrome wallet extension (8,000 users), Flutter mobile wallet (125 merged PRs), led EVM → PolkaVM migration (Rust resolc verifier for Blockscout). ### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

### Category

Infrastructure

### Project Summary

A one-command testnet developer suite for Zcash: a CLI faucet that pays shielded testnet TAZ with no account or captcha, and a one-command testnet wallet with address, QR, funding, and a payment watcher — built to remove the first-hour onboarding friction that blocks new Zcash developers and hackathon teams.


### Project Description

Getting testnet ZEC (TAZ) kept blocking new developers, hackathon teams, and Zecathon projects. The existing paths were slow: a 15–30 minute Rust build for zcash-devtool with no prebuilt binaries, zingolib tags with no files, a bare zkool2 binary, and WebZjs pre-Ironwood and not on npm — all before a first shielded transaction.

I built two MIT-licensed tools, both shipped and live on testnet in 30 Oct – 7 Nov 2026:

1. zcash-faucet — `npx zcash-faucet <address>`. No account, no captcha. Your machine mines a short Argon2id proof-of-work (about 10–60 seconds, 19 MiB memory), then 0.1 TAZ arrives as a real shielded transaction. Supports unified (utest1…), Sapling, and transparent addresses; rejects mainnet. The server wraps zcash-devtool and talks to the public testnet lightwalletd. It also has a regtest mode, a Docker/self-host option, and a 5-minute health monitor that opens a GitHub issue if the faucet is down or dry.

2. zcash-testnet-wallet — `npx zcash-testnet-wallet`. In about 2 minutes it gives you a prebuilt zcash-devtool, a fresh testnet wallet (keys local only), a utest1 address with a terminal QR code, 0.1 TAZ from the faucet, and balance. Commands: `balance`, `send <utest1…> 0.01 --memo "hi"`, `viewkey`, and `watch --ufvk <key> --memo order-42` — a payment watcher that fires on mined and on confirmed, once per transaction, from the viewing key alone, plus a JavaScript `watchPayments` API.

A portfolio index of all of this is at https://github.com/anukulpandey/zcash-pow (README only, created 7 Nov 2026).

Continuing work (not part of this request, not funded here): I plan to keep building developer tooling on Zcash, including create-zcash-dapp — a boilerplate / starter template for building a first Zcash dApp — and a second public testnet lightwalletd server (Zebra + Zaino), so developers are not dependent on a single public endpoint. None of this future work is claimed or funded by this proposal; this proposal is only for the faucet and wallet already shipped.


### Technical Approach (how you did it)

- zcash-faucet (v1.2.1, 26 commits, 30 Oct – 7 Nov 2026): Node CLI, zero npm dependencies in the client. Argon2id PoW as the default anti-abuse mechanism (Node 24 ships Argon2id natively), with per-address signed challenges and difficulty rising on claim spikes. GitHub device login was the v1.0.0 mechanism; after @strahncryptography flagged it on the forum on 30 Oct, I shipped v1.1.0 the same day (no token written to disk, server verifies the token belongs to the faucet app with no scopes and revokes it via the GitHub API right after the check) and v1.2.0 on 31 Oct making PoW the default, with GitHub login only as an optional fast lane. Server wraps zcash-devtool, talks to public lightwalletd testnet.zec.rocks. Live status page at https://zcash-faucet.vercel.app, live chain stats at https://zcash-faucet.vercel.app/api/stats.

- zcash-testnet-wallet (v0.1.1, 4 commits, 7 Nov 2026): Node CLI wrapping prebuilt zcash-devtool binaries for macOS (darwin-arm64 and darwin-x64 via optional dependencies, Node >=22.13). Creates a local wallet, prints a utest1 address and QR, funds it from the faucet, and watches payments from a unified full viewing key. Limits stated at launch: macOS only for now, watcher sees payments only once mined (mempool stage is future work, not claimed here), single public testnet lightwalletd.

- Iteration in public: all of this was built and revised on the Zcash Forum as @anuna, including the security-driven redesign above, with usage numbers posted publicly.

### Application Owners (@octocat, @octocat1)

### Organization or Individual Name

### Additional Team Members


### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

Active ZCAP member and participant in the Zcash Community Forum

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

75,000

### Category

Research & Development

### Project Summary

I'm requesting $75,000 for my responsible disclosure of [CVE-2026-104423](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-104423), a High severity remote DoS vulnerability in Zebra that could have cut off the wallets, exchanges and miners relying on it from the rest of the network.

At almost no cost, an attacker could stop every reachable Zebra node from syncing with the Zcash blockchain.

The Zcash Foundation published the [advisory](https://github.com/ZcashFoundation/zebra/security/advisories/GHSA-2p4c-3q4q-p463) crediting me as the sole reporter.


### Project Description

Zcash has come a long way in ten years, and a lot of that progress is owed to the people committed to making the network stronger.

Special thanks to Taylor Hornby.

**The report**

In July I discovered and responsibly disclosed [GHSA-2p4c-3q4q-p463](https://github.com/ZcashFoundation/zebra/security/advisories/GHSA-2p4c-3q4q-p463) ("Uncapped shielded verification cost lets peer-pushed V6 transactions stall block verification"); **a High severity remote DoS in Zebra version 6.2.0**

Before Zebra accepts a transaction from another node, it needs to verify it. Unfortunately, on versions before 6.2.1 it did the expensive verification checks first and left the cheap ones for later (like whether the transaction paid a fee), and because Zebra checks new blocks in the same line as these transactions, real blocks ended up waiting behind them.

**What an attack looked like**

1. An attacker connects to a Zebra node as an ordinary peer, which the advisory notes requires "no authentication or special privileges."
2. They send transactions carrying fake proofs, which can be produced very easily on an ordinary computer without paying any fee.
3. The Zebra node does the expensive work of checking every single one of them before it can reject them, and new blocks wait in the same line behind that work.
4. The node stops syncing for as long as the attacker keeps sending these fake transactions, and the attacker can do the same to every reachable Zebra node at once.

Since the network now runs on Zebra, the wallets, exchanges and miners relying on those nodes would have stopped seeing new blocks until the attack ended.

**Disclosure and fix**

I submitted the advisory on July 20 and messaged Pili and Conrado from the Zcash Foundation on the Z3 Signal group, and less than two days later, on July 22, the fix was merged and shipped in [Zebra 6.2.1](https://github.com/ZcashFoundation/zebra/releases/tag/v6.2.1), which now checks fees before proofs and disconnects peers that send invalid ones. The Foundation rated it High and published the advisory on August 17 crediting me as the sole reporter, and [CVE-2026-104423](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-104423) was assigned on October 2. Zakura's [1.0.3 release notes](https://zakura.com/announcements/zakura-1-0-3/) credit the report as well.

I hope that coinholders rewarding this report encourages more people to look closely at the software Zcash runs on and bring what they find to the teams who can fix it.


### Technical Approach (how you did it)

While building on Zcash, I spent a lot of time studying the Zebra node, especially how it takes a transaction from the mempool into a confirmed block, since I wanted to understand what checks Zebra runs on a transaction, and in what order. 

While working through it with an LLM, I learned that new blocks and incoming transactions were verified in the same queue, so new blocks could end up waiting behind them.

Suspecting a weakness in this design, I used an LLM-assisted auditing harness to find attack paths around this seam, and it turned out a peer could fill that queue with transactions carrying fake proofs, which is how I discovered the vulnerability

From there I built a complete proof of concept against a live Regtest network to confirm the attack, after which I submitted the advisory to the Zcash Foundation on July 20 with the PoC and vulnerability details


### Time Period of Work Completion

Q3 2026, July 2026 - August 2026

### Total Budget (USD)

$0

### Budget Breakdown

Security researchers participating in bug bounties are paid on the merit of their disclosure, not a fixed salary/budget. 

### Previous Funding

No

### Previous Funding Details

_No response_

### Other Funding Sources

No

### Other Funding Sources Details

_No response_

### Success Metrics

- Accepted and published by ZFND Security as a [High severity vulnerability](https://github.com/ZcashFoundation/zebra/security/advisories/GHSA-2p4c-3q4q-p463) (CVSS 7.5), with sole reporter credit and [CVE-2026-104423](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-104423) assigned.
- Attack path confirmed: any malicious peer could stall a Zebra node's syncing very cheaply for as long as the attack continued.
- Reported and fixed in [Zebra 6.2.1](https://github.com/ZcashFoundation/zebra/releases/tag/v6.2.1) before NU6.3 (Ironwood) activated on Mainnet ensuring nodes upgraded on time and weren't exposed.


### Proof of completion

- Zakura 1.0.3 release notes crediting my report: https://zakura.com/announcements/zakura-1-0-3/

- [x] I understand all grants are valued in USD but will be disbursed in Shielded ZEC. I acknowledge and accept that disbursement amounts may fluctuate based on the ZEC/USD exchange rate at the time of payment.

### Application Owners (@octocat, @octocat1)

@kenbak

### Organization or Individual Name

Kenbak

### Additional Team Members

N/A

### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

Previous Applicant

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

125000

### Category

Infrastructure

### Project Summary

ZecBlock (formerly CipherScan) is a production Zcash block explorer and data platform at [zecblock.com](https://zecblock.com). This application covers one quarter of completed, previously unfunded work (August – November 2026) that made Zcash chain data queryable by people, developers and AI clients: Zift research, a public API and MCP server, multi-venue cross-chain data, network observability, and the security response that kept it all safe through October.

### Project Description

In Q3, coinholders funded the foundation: the Rust indexer, privacy intelligence, mining analytics and the data bot. This quarter built on it, so Zcash data can now be **queried, integrated and built on**, not only browsed.

This application covers six completed work packages that are not part of any ZCG milestone or the Q3 grant.

### 1. Zift: AI research and SQL workspace

[zecblock.com/zift](https://zecblock.com/zift) lets anyone ask a question about Zcash in plain language and get an answer backed by real SQL over public chain data. Every number traces back to its query.

- Questions are compiled into one reviewed, read-only SELECT. Answers include a table, a chart chosen for the data (rankings, daily series, shares) and a units note.
- **21 public datasets**: blocks, transactions, pool flows, daily pool history, supply and issuance, mining pools, mining software, block timing, reorgs, orphaned blocks, cross-chain swaps, value pools, transparent UTXO set and coin-days, address summaries and activity, and labels.
- Datasets are added in reviewed batches, and each must pass a publication gate before it can be queried. Production answers for each new dataset were checked against direct SQL and matched.
- Direct SQL mode, plus clarifying questions and follow-ups for longer research.
- Privacy: no account needed, no IP-derived identifiers stored, research saved only in the browser, and optional anonymous answer ratings.
- Safe to expose publicly: SQL is validated at the parser level (allow-listed datasets only, row and time limits), runs under a read-only database role, and has site-wide quotas.

### 2. Open data layer: `/v1` API, OpenAPI and public MCP server

- **Stable `/v1` API**: additive-only compatibility policy and generated OpenAPI 1.0.0 docs at [zecblock.com/docs](https://zecblock.com/docs). Public reads need no key. Monetary values are exact zatoshi strings.
- **Public read-only MCP server** at `/v1/mcp` with **22 tools**, so any AI client (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and others) can query Zcash directly:
  - blocks, transactions, addresses and mempool
  - supply, fees, halving and network accounting
  - pool history and activity, reorgs
  - cross-chain swaps and venues
  - Zift's `sql_catalogue` and `sql_query`
  - Included in the Docker MCP catalog.
- Search by shortened transaction id or block hash, freshness headers (`X-ZecBlock-Indexed-Height`, data age in blocks), and IndexNow notifications so search engines pick up new blocks and transactions quickly.

### 3. Multi-venue cross-chain data

- **Full NEAR Intents history**: 290,009 records back to March 30, 2025, fully traversed and reconciled, with continuous live sync. Totals: 277,787 successful swaps, $2.57B reported volume, 5.74M ZEC.
- **Swap outcomes**: completed, refunded, failed, processing or incomplete deposit. Unfunded quotes are excluded, so counts reflect real swaps.
- **Maya Protocol** (14,372 records since May 2025) and **THORChain** (1,361 since October 2026) added as venues with five-minute sync, plus a venue comparison that ranks venues side by side without summing them.
- Transaction pages tag Maya and THORChain swaps, alongside the existing NEAR bridge badges.
- Pair rankings by swap count, USD or ZEC. The data bot now also posts large Maya and THORChain swaps and names each swap's venue.

### 4. Network and consensus observability

- **Chain-qualified node census**: peers are verified against the chain before they are counted. Shows Tor availability, client recognition (Zebra, Zakura, Zebend, Seeder) and regional census vantage points. 482 active nodes observed today.
- **Gossip topology** with globe and map views.
- **Competing-block capture**: continuous collection of orphaned blocks, a daily orphan-rate chart, and measured capture coverage. Partner observers (zecminingpool.com) report orphans our own nodes never saw.
- **Miner data quality**: fixed funding-stream outputs being counted as miners and repaired historical summaries. Added readable coinbase messages and miner header time vs. the time ZecBlock first saw each block.
- **Attestation monitor** for independently reproduced Zero Indexer builds.

### 5. ZecBlock relaunch and public data surfaces

- **CipherScan → ZecBlock** (October 1): new identity, typography and design system across mainnet, testnet and API. Zero downtime, with old URLs redirecting.
- **Governance hub** ([/governance](https://zecblock.com/governance)): automatic discovery of every coinholder vote round, published results with verification, and a beginner voting guide. This extends Q3's single NU7 vote page to all rounds.
- **Live data cards** ([/cards](https://zecblock.com/cards)): 17 branded, always-current fact cards to share or embed.
- **Learn hub** with a developer onboarding path. Shielded pool activity charts with count, share and image export. ZEC/BTC history.


### 6. Security response and data integrity ("Black October")

October brought a wave of critical vulnerabilities across the Node.js and Linux stack that the explorer runs on, at the same time as large automated traffic attacks. The work was to keep ZecBlock and its public API safe, online and correct for every user throughout.

- **Node2Shell / HTTP2Shell (CVE-2026-111497, Brotli remote code execution).** Inventoried every Node process on all eight servers and patched them all to a fixed Node build. Traced which API parsers could reach the vulnerable decoder. Redeployed every frontend once the hosting provider's patched runtime became available.
- **API dependency vulnerabilities.** Patched an unauthenticated compressed-request crash in the API's body parser (CVE-2026-111181) and validation-library issues. Public JSON reads are now bounded: 2 MiB maximum, 8-second deadline, and size limits checked before validation.
- **Outbound credential boundary.** Internal service credentials are now attached only to their exact configured origin and never follow redirects. Covered by regression tests.
- **Dependency audit.** Took four npm lockfiles to zero known findings and removed seven unused dependencies. Shipped Rust fixes (Tokio, rustls-webpki, zstd) to every writer, collector and the standby, verifying the binary hash on each host.
- **Host hardening across eight servers.** Rolling kernel and OS patches with reboots, MPTCP disabled everywhere, default-deny firewalls where they were missing, and an SSH access review of all eight servers.

No user data, keys or funds were involved. ZecBlock holds no viewing keys and has no user accounts.

### Scope intentionally excluded

- **ZCG Milestone 4**: NU7 support (accounting, block speed, upgrades hub, readiness), shielded rate tracking, infrastructure scaling (HA, failover, monitoring, load testing) and the Zakura node migration.
- **Earlier ZCG milestones** (M1–M3.5).
- **Work funded in Q3**: indexer, privacy intelligence, mining analytics, valuation, Network Pulse, the original data bot and the NU7 vote page.
- **Crosslink explorer** work.
- **CipherPay** and other Atmosphere Labs products.
- **Unreleased research.**

### Technical Approach (how you did it)

ZecBlock uses two public repositories:

- [Kenbak/zecblock](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock): Next.js/React, Express API, PostgreSQL, Redis, scheduled jobs, the MCP server and the Zift worker.
- [Kenbak/zecblock-rust](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock-rust): Rust indexer reading node state, plus collectors.

**Zift.** A separate analytics host receives a filtered PostgreSQL logical-replication feed of reviewed public tables. A model turns each question into SQL. A parser-level policy then checks the SQL (allow-listed datasets, no functions such as `now()`, row and time limits) before a read-only role runs it. Results are checked against expected units before the answer is shown.

**MCP.** The server reuses the same `/v1` readers and Zift's SQL path, so AI clients get the same data and limits as the website.

**Cross-chain.** Bounded workers ingest NEAR Intents, Maya and THORChain with fair pagination, retry limits, weekly status rechecks and explicit coverage metadata.

**Network data.** Node census results are checked against the chain before publication. Orphan capture combines our own observers with partner reports and publishes how much of the network it covers.

**Releases.** Every release passes CI, security audit, CodeQL and Docker checks, followed by exact-commit deployment and host verification.

### Time Period of Work Completion

August - November

### Total Budget (USD)

125000

### Budget Breakdown

- Compensation:
  - $(USD): $125,000
  - Justification: Fixed retrospective valuation of six completed work packages covering approximately one quarter of full-time development (August - November): Zift research workspace, open data layer (v1 API, OpenAPI and MCP server), multi-venue cross-chain data, network and consensus observability, the ZecBlock relaunch, and the October security response and data-integrity fixes.
- Technology/Software:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: No separate technology expense requested.
- Infrastructure/Hosting:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: Hosting expenses covered by ZCG are excluded. The dedicated analytics host is not claimed.
- Services/Contractors:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: No contractors included.
- Other:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: No domains, marketing, or future expenses included.
- Total $(USD): $125,000

### Previous Funding

Yes

### Previous Funding Details

**Q3 2026 Coinholder Retroactive Grant (CipherScan, #47):** $375,000, paid October 16, 2026, covering November 2025 – August 2026. This application covers only later work and re-claims nothing from Q3.

### Other Funding Sources

Yes

### Other Funding Sources Details

- **ZCG grant (CipherScan/ZecBlock):** $73,500 approved, $58,800 paid through M3.5. M4 ($14,700) covers the items excluded above.

### Success Metrics

A block explorer is the heartbeat monitor of a blockchain. This quarter, ZecBlock also became a way to **ask** that heartbeat questions. A person can ask Zift, a developer can call `/v1`, and an AI agent can connect over MCP, and all three get the same verified data.

- **Data people can question.** Zift answers Zcash research questions with the query and source shown. Its 21 datasets range from supply and mining to orphans, swaps and coin-days.
- **Zcash in AI tools.** Any MCP client can read Zcash from a public, keyless, read-only server with 22 tools, including the same SQL access Zift uses.
- **Cross-chain clarity.** NEAR Intents, Maya and THORChain flows into and out of Zcash, side by side: 290K+ NEAR records with outcomes, 14K+ Maya, 1.3K+ THORChain.
- **Network health in public.** A chain-qualified census of 482 active nodes, and orphan capture that partner miners now contribute to. Before this, only node operators could see this data.
- **Governance transparency.** Every coinholder vote round, including this one, is tracked automatically with verifiable results.
- **Safe through Black October.** Every server, runtime and dependency was patched through the October vulnerability wave. Two bot fleets were contained without blocking real users, and a decade-old Sprout fee error was corrected for the whole chain.

### Platform scale (November 2026)
- 2,038 commits across the two public repositories (1,829 explorer, 209 indexer); 806 of them since August 15 (709 explorer, 97 indexer).
- 59 public page routes, a stable `/v1` API with OpenAPI, and a 22-tool MCP server.
- Live mainnet, testnet and Crosslink explorers, public lightwalletd and Tor hidden services.

### Community reach
- **40,474 visitors and 99,437 page views** during this application period (August – November 7, 2026).

### Proof of completion

- Repository/Commit:
  - [ZecBlock explorer / API / MCP / Zift](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock)
  - [ZecBlock Rust indexer](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock-rust)
  - **Zift:** [#181](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/181) workspace, [#193](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/193) agent, [#184](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/184) charts, [#206](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/206) publication gate, [#203](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/203) no IP identifiers, dataset batches [#207](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/207) [#213](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/213) [#215](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/215) [#217](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/217) [#228](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/228) [#231](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/231)
  - **Open data:** [#173](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/173) public MCP, [#199](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/199) MCP SQL tools, [#174](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/174) Docker MCP catalog, [#235](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/235) OpenAPI, [#175](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/175) IndexNow
  - **Cross-chain:** [#173](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/173) Maya/THORChain venues, [#176](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/176) transaction venue tags, [#242](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/242) venue swap posts
  - **Network:** [#153](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/153) topology, [#252](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/252) regional census, [#118](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/118) orphan rates, [#258](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/258) partner observers, [#260](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/260) daily orphan chart, [#125](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/125) miner attribution, [#196](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/196) header time vs first seen
  - **Security and integrity:** [#145](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/145) dependency audit, [#142](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/142) Node security update, [#157](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/157) API dependency fixes and bounded reads, [#160](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/160) credential boundary, [#134](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/134) cache efficiency, [zecblock-rust #34](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock-rust/pull/34) Rust security fixes, [zecblock-rust #37](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock-rust/pull/37) Sprout fees, [#218](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/218) Sprout fee display
  - **Relaunch:** [#96](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/96) ZecBlock launch, [#167](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/167) governance, [#161](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/161) learn, [#164](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/164) pool activity, [#241](https://github.com/Kenbak/zecblock/pull/241) data cards

### Project Summary

We added Zcash to Any Wallet Kit, an open-source (Apache-2.0) multichain wallet SDK, so any wallet built on it can hold, send and swap ZEC: transparent accounts compatible with Zashi/ZODL and Ledger, mainnet sending, and swaps between ZEC and 29 chains through NEAR Intents.

### Project Description

Any Wallet Kit (AWK) is an open-source TypeScript SDK that teams use to ship self-custodial wallets on React Native, web and Node. It covers 36 networks and 25 protocol modules, and every transaction is decoded and simulated before signing.

This application covers the Zcash integration we completed in October 2026. Before it, a wallet team building on AWK had no way to offer ZEC; now ZEC is a first-class chain in the kit:

- ZEC accounts derived from the same seed as the rest of the wallet, with addresses that match Zashi/ZODL, YWallet, Ledger and Trezor, so users can import or move funds without surprises.
- Sending ZEC on mainnet with fee and recipient safety checks.
- ZEC in the swap catalog: users of any AWK-based wallet can swap into and out of ZEC from EVM chains, Solana, TON, Tron and others in one step through NEAR Intents. This is a new on-ramp into ZEC for multichain users.

The package is published on npm as @anywalletkit/wallet-zcash. Shielded support is the next step: we plan to propose a reusable shielded (Ironwood) layer built on the official Zcash SDKs to ZCG separately; it is not part of this retroactive request.

### Technical Approach (how you did it)

- **Keys and addresses:** BIP-44 path m/44'/133'/0'/0/i for transparent t1 addresses, the same receiver as Zashi/ZODL, YWallet, Ledger and Trezor; keys and t1 encoding cross-checked against independent implementations and live mainnet addresses.
- **Transactions:** v5 transactions (ZIP-225) with ZIP-244 txid and sighash, built and signed in pure TypeScript. Pinned by two mined mainnet transactions: parse/serialize round-trip, txid equality, and every on-chain signature verifies over the digest we compute (and fails on a tampered amount). ZIP-317 fees, own coin selection, ZIP-203 expiry, consensus branch IDs from the tip height up to NU6.3.
- **Safety:** fee cap (0.01 ZEC by default), exact recipient and amount checks, change ownership checks. This release is transparent-only: sending to shielded addresses (u1, zs1, zc) is not supported yet and is refused with a clear error instead of failing silently.
- **Testing:** 50 unit tests, a conformance suite shared with the other chains in the kit, and 238 checks inside the React Native (Hermes) runtime that wallets actually run on, including derivation, signing and ZIP-244 verification.
- **Transports:** public block explorers (Blockchair, Zcash Blockbook) with failover for balances, UTXOs, history and broadcast.
- **Swaps:** ZEC added to the swap catalog; NEAR Intents (1Click) quotes and swaps in both directions with refunds to the source chain.
- **Release:** first shipped October 18, 2026; published on npm as @anywalletkit/wallet-zcash (current version 0.5.1), Apache-2.0, with CONTRIBUTING.md in the repository.

October 2026 (first shipped October 18, 2026; current release 0.5.1 on November 2, 2026)

- [x] I understand all grants are valued in USD but will be disbursed in Shielded ZEC. I acknowledge and accept that disbursement amounts may fluctuate based on the ZEC/USD exchange rate at the time of payment.

### Application Owners

@AArnott

### Organization or Individual Name

Andrew Arnott (nerdcash)

### Additional Team Members

None

### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

Zcash Community Forum

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

$20,000

### Category

Infrastructure

### Project Summary

zcash-payment-service lets any merchant accept shielded Zcash with no middlemen and no fees. It is a free, MIT-licensed, self-hosted service that holds only a viewing key, so payments go straight from payer to merchant. It ships plugins for WooCommerce, Medusa, Vendure, Easy Digital Downloads, and PrestaShop, a hosted pay page, and a one-command HTTPS deploy, and it is already the payment backend for MoneyStream on mainnet. First stable release: v0.1.0.

### Project Description

Cryptocurrency promises payments with no middlemen and no fees, yet most payment processors are provider-hosted and charge fees, so merchants rarely get that benefit. zcash-payment-service removes every third party from the transaction. The payer sends shielded ZEC directly to the merchant's own wallet, and the merchant's own server confirms it using only a unified incoming viewing key (UIVK). The service can see payments but can never spend them. It is a small Docker container or an embeddable Rust crate. It gives each checkout a fresh shielded address, scans the chain through lightwalletd, and sends the merchant's app an HMAC-signed webhook when a payment arrives. There are no fees, no accounts, and no provider.

It is in production on mainnet as the payment backend for MoneyStream's paid tiers (https://moneystreamapp.com), which accept only Zcash. Example verifiable payment: https://zecblock.com/tx/63dce15bdc607a2041797c11e50fe3dce1fa4b116fbf8515620a39e5552b5a62

Merchants on WooCommerce (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#45), Medusa (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#55), Vendure (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#58), Easy Digital Downloads (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#69), and PrestaShop (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#75) can install a plugin instead of writing code. Each checkout gets a payment link, a QR code, and a hosted pay page that follows the payment live (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#42). With REQUIRED_CONFIRMATIONS set, the service reports the amount received at each confirmation depth, and every plugin marks an order received but pending confirmation until it is confirmed, so merchants choose their own risk level (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#71, nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#72, nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#77). A docker compose file with Caddy brings up the service and pay page with automatic HTTPS in one command (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#63), and a VPS guide walks a merchant from an empty server to production, including backups and upgrades (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#67).

It complements hosted processors such as CipherPay: this service is for merchants who would rather run one more container than pay fees. A Node/TypeScript client (@nerdcash/zcash-payment-client) and an open-source demo store (video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OIlkqLVTn0w) make custom integrations simple.

Community interest: https://x.com/aarnott/status/2117453042115326113

I intend to continue goodwill maintenance of the service; that is not a funded deliverable of this proposal.

### Technical Approach (how you did it)

Rust service built on the published crates.io releases of librustzcash's zcash_client_backend (0.25.0) and zcash_client_sqlite (0.23.0), with its own viewing-key scanner and sandblasting spam filter. Related but not claimed here: the upstream UIVK import PR (zcash/librustzcash#3206) belongs to the separate Nerdbank.Cryptocurrencies and librustzcash fork proposal. HTTP API and signed webhooks. Confirmation-depth balances are derived from receipt heights, so changing REQUIRED_CONFIRMATIONS rebuilds them automatically, and the webhook worker queues every change found during reorg and overlap reconciliation. Store plugins are in PHP (WooCommerce, Easy Digital Downloads, PrestaShop) and TypeScript (Medusa, Vendure). Multi-arch (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64) images on GHCR, versioned from release tags: v0.1.0 at https://github.com/nerdcash/zcash-payment-service/releases/tag/v0.1.0. mdBook docs at https://nerdcash.github.io/zcash-payment-service/. The npm client is published through GitHub OIDC trusted publishing with provenance. CI runs 135 Rust tests, each plugin's unit tests, and a Docker end-to-end checkout test per plugin, behind one required gate (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#68).

Selected merged work (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service):
- Store plugins: WooCommerce (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#45), Medusa v2 (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#55), Vendure (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#58), Easy Digital Downloads (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#69), PrestaShop (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#75)
- Hosted pay page and payment links (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#42)
- Confirmation-depth balances across the service, npm client, and plugins (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#71, nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#72, nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#77)
- One-command production deploy with docker compose and Caddy, automatic HTTPS (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#63), plus a VPS guide (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#67)
- Docker end-to-end checkout tests per plugin and one required CI gate (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#68)
- First stable release v0.1.0 as multi-arch GHCR images (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#43); deploy files pinned to 0.1.0 (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#79)
- Webhook reliability fixes (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#25, nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#44, nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#51)
- SECURITY.md (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#38) and docs comparing with CipherPay and BTCPay Server (nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#39)

### Time Period of Work Completion

June 2026 to November 2026

### Total Budget (USD)

$20,000

### Budget Breakdown

- Compensation:
  - $(USD): 20,000
  - Justification: 100 hours at $200/hour, covering design, the Rust service and its viewing-key scanner, docs, the npm client, the demo store, the five store plugins, the pay page, confirmation-depth balances, and the compose deploy.
- Technology/Software:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: None claimed.
- Infrastructure/Hosting:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: None claimed.
- Services/Contractors:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: None claimed.
- Other:
  - $(USD): 0
  - Justification: None claimed.
- Total $(USD): 20,000

### Previous Funding

No

### Previous Funding Details

No previous funding from the Coinholder program. For transparency: two Zcash Foundation Minor Grants for Nerdbank.Zcash (.NET). (1) Unified Address parsing and construction library for .NET, $750, approved April 17, 2023. (2) Full lightwallet functionality for .NET, $18,000, approved October 2023 and completed February 19, 2024. Neither overlaps this scope.

### Other Funding Sources

No

### Other Funding Sources Details

None

### Success Metrics

- In production on mainnet as the payment backend for MoneyStream's paid tiers (merchant 1, owner-operated). Example verifiable payment: https://zecblock.com/tx/63dce15bdc607a2041797c11e50fe3dce1fa4b116fbf8515620a39e5552b5a62
- Shipped: MIT service with its first stable release (v0.1.0, multi-arch GHCR images), plugins for five store platforms with end-to-end tests, hosted pay page, one-command HTTPS deploy and VPS guide, mdBook guide, npm package (0.1.0 and 0.1.1), demo store, demo video
- Store plugins for WooCommerce, Medusa, Vendure, Easy Digital Downloads, and PrestaShop, with confirmation-aware order handling
- Community interest on X: https://x.com/aarnott/status/2117453042115326113
- Outreach to outside merchants is ongoing

### Proof of completion

- Repository/Commit:
  - [zcash-payment-service](https://github.com/nerdcash/zcash-payment-service) - the MIT-licensed payment service
  - [Store plugins](https://github.com/nerdcash/zcash-payment-service#store-plugins) - WooCommerce, Medusa, Vendure, Easy Digital Downloads, PrestaShop
  - [zcash-payment-demo-store](https://github.com/nerdcash/zcash-payment-demo-store) - open-source demo store
- Publication:
  - [@nerdcash/zcash-payment-client on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nerdcash/zcash-payment-client) - Node/TypeScript client
  - [mdBook docs](https://nerdcash.github.io/zcash-payment-service/) - documentation site
  - [Demo video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OIlkqLVTn0w) - checkout walkthrough
