### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

Jason McGee

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

$800,000

### Category

Infrastructure

### Project Summary

This project enabled the first practical way to “encrypt Bitcoin” at scale by converting BTC into shielded ZEC using permissionless smart contract–based execution.

By integrating Zcash with Near Intents, users were able to route Bitcoin into shielded ZEC using permissionless smart contract–based execution, with transaction execution verifiable on-chain. This shifted Zcash acquisition away from centralized exchanges, increased shielded adoption via the Orchard Pool, and unlocked new ecosystem integrations across wallets and DeFi applications.

The work is complete, live in production, and verifiable by the community.

### Project Description

## Encrypt Your Bitcoin

This work transformed “encrypting Bitcoin” from an abstract narrative into an observable, repeatable behavior.

Historically, acquiring Zcash relied heavily on centralized exchanges. Near Intents changed this by allowing users to convert Bitcoin into shielded ZEC using permissionless smart contract–based execution, with transaction execution verifiable on-chain.

During periods of peak activity, multiple BTC per second were converted into ZEC through Near Intents. This activity was publicly visible via the NEAR block explorer, creating a powerful adoption loop: users could see others encrypting Bitcoin in real time, reinforcing trust, momentum, and participation.

### Shielded Adoption and Orchard Pool Growth

Near Intents did not simply improve access to ZEC. It changed where users entered the Zcash ecosystem.

ZEC acquired through Near Intents was routed directly into the Orchard Pool, increasing shielded supply and strengthening Zcash’s privacy guarantees. This aligned new demand with Zcash’s core objective of maximizing shielded usage and improving long-term network privacy.

Public Orchard Pool metrics show a sustained increase in shielded ZEC supply following the Near Intents integration, as tracked on the ZecHub dashboard - https://zechub.wiki/dashboard. 

### Ecosystem Impact

The ability to encrypt Bitcoin via Near Intents unlocked broader second-order effects:

- Wallets and applications such as Infinex and Rhea Finance rely on Near Intents as backend infrastructure for Zcash.
- Near Intents functions as shared infrastructure, enabling decentralized finance workflows for Zcash that previously did not exist.
- Zcash’s historical dependence on centralized exchanges for liquidity was meaningfully reduced, mitigating systemic risk.

This impact extends beyond individual users to the broader Zcash ecosystem.

## Retroactive Scope and No Future Commitments

This application is submitted in recognition of already completed and publicly released work and does not create any obligation for future delivery, maintenance, or ongoing support. The integration is provided on an “as is” basis, without service-level commitments or guarantees.

### Technical Approach (how you did it)

This application covers completed engineering work to integrate Zcash (ZEC) into NEAR Intents, OmniBridge, and PoA bridging infrastructure, with full support for both unshielded and shielded (Orchard) ZEC flows. It also includes ongoing operational and customer support for the Zashi wallet.

All work described below is complete, deployed, and in production.

**NEAR Intents Integration**

Completed work to make ZEC a first-class asset within NEAR Intents included:

- Enabling ZEC across solvers, the message bus, and the 1Click API
- Adding ZEC to the Intents routing system
- Implementing solver-side liquidity support so ZEC can be quoted and executed end-to-end
- Ensuring compatibility across quoting, execution, and settlement flows

This allows ZEC to participate fully in Intents-based abstracted user flows.

**OmniBridge and PoA Bridge Integration**

Implemented full ZEC support across both OmniBridge and the PoA bridge, including:

- ZEC address generation
- Unshielded transaction construction and submission
- Shielded transaction construction and submission
- Transaction verification and confirmation tracking
- Required bridge-side plumbing for both OmniBridge and PoA architectures

This work enables reliable ZEC deposits and withdrawals across supported bridge paths.

**Shielded (Orchard) ZEC Support**

Supporting shielded ZEC flows required additional ecosystem-level work:

- Implemented a dedicated Rust crate using librustzcash
- Supported Orchard transaction construction, proof generation, and verification
- Exposed this functionality to the TypeScript stack via NAPI-RS bindings
- Integrated shielded flows into existing bridge and Intents infrastructure

This addressed the lack of a native TypeScript SDK for Orchard transaction handling.

**Infrastructure Components**

The project includes and operates the following production infrastructure:

- Self-hosted Zcash nodes and RPC endpoints
- Zcash indexers
- A light client component for OmniBridge
- PoA bridge RPC and indexing infrastructure
- Service integration across the solver stack, message bus, and 1Click API

**Zashi Wallet Support and Operations**

In addition to protocol and infrastructure work, we provided direct operational support for the Zashi wallet, including:

- High-touch customer support via a priority queue
- Rapid triage of Zashi-related user issues
- Expedited resolution of cases impacting ZEC deposits and withdrawals

This reduced user-facing downtime and offloaded incident response from other ecosystem teams.

**Privacy Preservation and Orchard Impact**

This work preserves and strengthens Zcash’s privacy guarantees by:

- Enabling shielded (Orchard) deposits and withdrawals as first-class flows
- Allowing users to transact without exposing amounts or counterparties on-chain
- Preserving end-to-end privacy across bridge and Intents execution paths

By making shielded usage practical and reliable, this integration increases Orchard transaction activity and contributes to a larger effective shielded supply, strengthening the privacy set for the network.

**Zcash-Specific Constraints and Workarounds**

Key constraints encountered included limited documentation for shielded flows and the absence of a native TypeScript SDK for Orchard support.

These were addressed by:

- Building a Rust-based implementation on top of librustzcash
- Exposing functionality to the TypeScript stack via NAPI-RS
- Operating custom Zcash infrastructure to ensure production reliability

## Licensing and Code Availability

This application is submitted under a retroactive grant program in recognition of previously completed and deployed work. The integration described in this proposal has already been delivered and operates as part of a production system.

As such, this grant does not introduce new software deliverables or development outputs. Certain components of the system, including infrastructure, execution logic, solver coordination, and operational tooling, are proprietary and form part of a commercial offering.

Where applicable, the integration relies on publicly available smart contracts and open blockchain standards. However, this application does not propose the release or licensing of proprietary production code as a grant deliverable.

**Maintenance and Sustainability**

Ongoing maintenance requirements are relatively low and primarily driven by Zcash network upgrades and compatibility changes.

In steady state, the system can be maintained by approximately two developers on a part-time basis, with additional incident response as needed.

This description is provided for informational purposes only and does not constitute a commitment to provide future maintenance or support.

**Impact if Maintenance Ceases**

If maintenance were to stop entirely:

- Support for new Zcash transaction formats and network upgrades would degrade over time
- Failure rates for deposits and withdrawals would increase
- Reliability of ZEC flows would eventually break, negatively impacting users and ecosystem integrations

Continued light maintenance ensures long-term reliability for ZEC users across bridges and Intents.

### Time Period of Work Completion

Scope and Duration of Completed Work

Total duration: ~5 calendar months of core engineering work, plus ongoing support and maintenance.

Work breakdown:

~1 month: Unshielded ZEC support, including PoA bridge integration

~1 month: Shielded ZEC support, including PoA bridge integration

~3 months: OmniBridge integration for ZEC

Additional effort:

Solver, routing, and 1Click enablement within NEAR Intents

Ongoing Zashi wallet support and incident response

### Total Budget (USD)

$800,000

### Budget Breakdown

The requested amount reflects both the direct cost of delivering this work and the significant ecosystem value it created.

- Compensation:
  - $(USD): $400,000
  - Justification: Covers approximately five months of senior engineering effort across multiple complex workstreams, including OmniBridge integration, PoA bridge support, NEAR Intents enablement, and full unshielded and shielded (Orchard) ZEC support. This includes system design, implementation, debugging, production hardening, and live incident response. The work required deep Zcash-specific expertise (librustzcash, Orchard transaction construction and verification) combined with cross-chain protocol and infrastructure experience. This reflects market-rate compensation for senior protocol and infrastructure engineers delivering production-grade systems.
- Technology/Software:
  - $(USD): $85,000
  - Justification: Covers development tooling, build systems, CI/CD infrastructure, security and monitoring software, and supporting tooling required for Rust and TypeScript development, NAPI-RS bindings, and cross-language integration. Also includes internal tooling to support Zcash transaction workflows, testing, and validation in production environments.
- Infrastructure/Hosting:
  - $(USD): $175,000
  - Justification: Covers operation of production Zcash infrastructure, including self-hosted Zcash nodes, RPC endpoints, indexers, light client components for OmniBridge, PoA bridge RPC and indexing infrastructure, and supporting cloud resources required for reliable deposits, withdrawals, and shielded transaction execution.
- Services/Contractors:
  - $(USD): $100,000
  - Justification: Covers external services and specialized support used during development and operations, including security reviews, infrastructure support, and specialized consulting related to Zcash transaction handling, reliability, and production readiness. These services reduced delivery risk and accelerated delivery.
- Other:
  - $(USD): $40,000
  - Justification: Covers operational overhead directly related to delivery and sustained operation of the work, including incident response coordination, on-call support processes, documentation, and ecosystem-facing support activities such as high-touch Zashi wallet user support.
- Total $(USD): $800,000


### Previous Funding

No

### Other Funding Sources

No

_No response_

### Success Metrics 

Data as of 6 Feb 2026
- Total ZEC trading volume executed via NEAR Intents (all time): >$1,350,000,000
- Total BTC converted into ZEC via NEAR Intents (“Encrypt your Bitcoin” flows): >$155,000,000
- Total Zashi wallet volume enabled by NEAR Intents: >$475,000,000
- Public Orchard Pool metrics show sustained growth in shielded ZEC supply following the Near Intents integration (ZecHub dashboard)

### Proof of completion

- Other Evidence:
  - (https://zechub.wiki/dashboard) - Public dashboard tracking Orchard Pool shielded ZEC supply, showing growth during and following the Near Intents integration period.

### Category

### Project Summary

Zcash.me enables Zcash users to associate human-readable URLs to their Zcash addresses. They bring their own wallet to interact with other members in the address book.

### Project Description

Zcash.me is a web directory where Zcash users find and message each other. Users can join with any free Zcash address and add a custom username. They can choose which web links to show so others can recognize them. Each profile shows a username, Zcash address, creation date, last activity, and validity period ("good thru"). Verification extends the good thru date and shows that members are active and reachable. Unverified addresses eventually expire and are removed from the directory. 

The site lets users prepare anonymous messages through ZIP-321 URIs and approve them in their own wallets. Zcash.me does not conduct transactions on behalf of users. A referral field and dashboard encourage users to invite others. The goal is to promote direct, encrypted, and voluntary interactions between users and increase shielded transaction activity on-chain by helping them prepare messages approved through their preferred Zcash wallet.


### Technical Approach (how you did it)

We store the data in a Supabase table named public_profile.

The navigation is controlled by React Router with two views: the main directory and individual profiles under /:slug.

Our ZcashMessage component builds ZIP-321 URIs, tracks byte counts, and knows the selected recipient.

Profiles are removed from the directory after extended period of inactivity and failing to verify.

Zcash Address Verification:  
- User claims ownership of a Zcash address.  
- Zcash.me sends a code to that address.  
- User repeats the code.  
- Zcash.me confirms the user controls that address.  
- The profile displays a verification badge.  

Public Link Verification:  
- Zcash address verification is complete.  
- User claims ownership of a public account (e.g., x.com/satoshi).  
- The account profile includes a link to the user’s Zcash.me page (e.g., zcash.me/satoshi).  
- Zcash.me confirms the link, verifying that the same person controls both accounts.  
- The profile displays a verification badge.

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

8000

### Category

Infrastructure

### Project Summary

Sozu Capital is building the financial foundation for a new economic class: privacy-conscious, globally sovereign entrepreneurs. At the core is Souzu Cash (SZX) — a next-generation, privacy-first stable token built on Zcash’s zero-knowledge infrastructure, but pegged not to fiat, but to a decentralized, real-time Consumer Price Index (dCPI) that reflects the true cost of living worldwide.

With Souzu Cash, you don’t just store value — you preserve purchasing power. A kilo of rice costs the same amount of SZX in 2025 as it will in 2125. This isn’t “fiat 2.0” — it’s post-fiat.

We’re replacing surveillance coins and CBDCs with a non-inflationary, permissionless, censorship-resistant standard that empowers builders to launch, scale, and get paid — instantly and privately — in their own communities. Every user becomes a reporter of real prices, making the token value a mirror of global grassroots economies.

Sozu Capital = Zcash privacy × Bitcoin scarcity × CPI-pegged stability × unstoppable entrepreneurship.

### Project Description

Replace Fiat. Empower Builders. Preserve Freedom.
Sozu Capital exists to make fiat obsolete by giving everyday merchants and entrepreneurs a better way to earn, save, and grow, without surveillance, inflation, or permission.
The current system is broken:
	•	Merchants use Visa and Stripe not by choice, but because customers already trust them.
	•	Fiat currencies are inflating, centralized, and extractive.
	•	Stablecoins are gaining ground, but most are pegged to the very fiat currencies we want to escape.
	•	CBDCs are looming,  bringing surveillance and programmable compliance.
We are building a privacy-first, entrepreneur-led alternative that flips the entire system on its head, starting with the people who move the economy every day: merchants.

Sozu Pay is a crypto-native Stripe alternative.

It’s a simple payment link system that lets merchants:
	•	Accept payments in SZX stablecoin instantly.
	•	Bypass Visa/Stripe’s 3–5% fees, settlement delays, and KYC friction.
	•	Access same-day liquidity in local fiat (thorugh zkp2p).
	•	Earn passive yield (15–20% APY) by simply holding SZX, powered by lending pools and real-world yield strategies.

SZX isn’t just a way to get paid. It’s a way to preserve purchasing power, earn yield, and exit fiat forever.

key properties of SZX:
	•	Zero-knowledge privacy layer based on Zcash infrastructure.
	•	Pegged to a Decentralized Consumer Price Index (dCPI) driven by real-world price submissions from users across geographies.
	•	Non-inflationary: Supply is capped, with deflationary mechanisms built in.
	•	Permissionless & censorship-resistant: No one can freeze or surveil your money.
In 2125, a kilo of rice should still cost the same amount of SZX as it does today.
Real stability means real value over time, not a USD peg.

SZX comes with built-in DeFi-native incentives for merchants and users to hold, rather than dump:
	•	Deposit SZX into liquidity pools and earn 15–20% APY through low-risk, real-world yield strategies inspired by Blend Protocol.
	•	Merchants who use Sozu Pay automatically participate in this system by default — creating sticky adoption.
	•	Over time, this transforms SZX from a payment method into a yield-bearing, programmable savings vehicle.

We’re not just building tools we’re reprogramming economic incentives, and over time, this builds a parallel economic rail, decentralized, opt-in, and privacy-first, fueled by entrepreneurs, not states.

Zcash already solved one of the hardest problems in crypto: private transactions with cryptographic guarantees.

Sozu extends this power by:
	•	Wrapping Zcash-level privacy into a merchant-first UI/UX layer (Sozu Pay).
	•	Embedding proof-of-purchase and proof-of-income mechanisms that preserve compliance without exposing user data.
	•	Scaling trustless financial tools across borders, use cases, and devices, even where regulation is hostile or fiat infrastructure is broken.

We believe the future belongs to entrepreneurs who are private by default and sovereign by design.
Sozu Capital is the engine.
SZX is the currency.
Sozu Pay is the bridge.


### Technical Approach (how you did it)

# Sozu Capital: Technical Architecture and Product Overview

## Abstract

**SozuCash (SZX)** is an autonomous, open-source protocol for the measurement and exchange of decentralized value. It maintains purchasing-power stability via algorithmic governance and real-time commodity data, without reliance on fiat currency, central issuance, or discretionary control. SZX is a crypto-collateralized, algorithmically stabilized unit with **no fiat custody**. A controller sets a **Target Redemption Price (TRP)** near $1 and offers **mint/redemption at TRP** against a diversified **on-chain reserve**. **Arbitrage** around TRP, **risk-sensitive fees**, and a **surplus/insurance buffer** keep market price tight. **Junior risk capital** absorbs volatility; **senior SZX** acts as digital cash. Transfers can run in a **shielded layer**; economics remain transparent.

## Vision

**Sozu Capital** is building foundational financial infrastructure for a new economy, one where privacy, purchasing power, and protocolized governance replace fiat systems, surveillance finance, and inflationary currencies.

At its core is **Sozu Cash (SZX)** — a **Zcash-native**, privacy-preserving, decentralized stable-value protocol. It operates on a **Decentralized Stability Acquisitive Value Index (DSAVI)** and is designed to integrate seamlessly into the **EVM ecosystem** via smart contracts while retaining the unmatched privacy features of Zcash.

**SZX is not a financial product, but a protocolized measure of decentralized value — a successor to fiat money, not an imitation of it.**

## Design Principles

1. **No fiat, no banks**: only crypto collateral held by immutable contracts.
2. **Convertibility**: permissionless **mint/redeem vs. reserve** at TRP → hard arbitrage anchor.
3. **Overcollateralization**: live **Collateralization Ratio** (CR) above a risk floor; dynamic fees steer CR.
4. **Market-based stability**: traders earn on deviations; protocol only sets rules/fees/TRP.
5. **Loss socialization minimized**: **junior shares** take first loss; SZX remains senior.
6. **Graceful degradation**: circuit breakers, rate limits, and global settlement escape hatches.
7. **Privacy-ready**: shielded transfers optional; mint/redeem boundaries remain auditable.

# Protocol Summary

| Component             | Description                                                                                          |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **SZX Token**         | A non-inflationary stable asset pegged to DSAVI, stabilized via oracle data and cryptographic proofs |
| **DSAVI Index**       | A weighted oracle-fed cost-of-living index across essential human needs and global commodities       |
| **Zcash Reserve**     | Shielded ZEC holdings act as privacy-first collateral for SZX issuance                               |
| **Sozu Pay**          | Merchant-facing infrastructure that enables frictionless payments in SZX                             |
| **Oracle Network**    | Crowdsourced and staked validators providing real-world pricing data into DSAVI                      |
| **Staking and Yield** | SZX holders can earn protocol yield from transaction fees and staking mechanisms                     |

# Sozu Cash (SZX): A Stable Value Protocol

## Core Components

- **SZX** — the stable unit targeting $1.
- **Reserve Set 𝒞** — on-chain, liquid crypto assets (e.g., ETH, stETH, WBTC, LSTs, high-liquidity LP tokens), each with risk weight w_i and cap.
- **Sozu Shares (SZS)** — junior tranche absorbing reserve drawdowns; earns protocol surplus.
- **Controller** — on-chain policy computing **TRP**, **fees**, and **throughput caps** from prices/volatility/CR.
- **Mint/Redeem Module** — permissionless exchange SZX ↔ reserve basket at **TRP** (minus/plus fees).
- **Surplus Buffer** \mathcal{B} — collects stability & mint/redeem fees; backstops small shocks; funds buybacks.
- **Insurance Vault** — optional extra buffer funded by SZS stakers.
- **Oracles** — medianized, TWAP-hardened, multi-source for both SZX market price and reserve asset prices.
- **(Optional) Shielded Pool** — Aztec-style notes/stealth transfers; entry/exit via public bridge.

## DSAVI = Σ (wᵢ × Pᵢ)

- **Pᵢ**: Real-time oracle price of each basket item (e.g. rice, rent per m2, natural gas)
- **wᵢ**: Normalized utility weight per item
- **SZX**: 1 unit of DSAVI = cost of living stability

### Oracle-Sourced Categories:

1. **Essential Goods & Services (The Non-Negotiable Basket)**

   - **Food & Water:** Staple grains (rice, wheat), proteins, vegetables, cooking oil, salt, water.
   - **Housing:** Average cost per square meter for basic rental/purchase, utility costs (electricity, water, heating).
   - **Transportation:** Cost of public transit, fuel, short-distance taxi/ride-share.
   - **Healthcare:** Cost of common medicines, a standard doctor's visit.
   - **Communications:** Cost of a mobile data plan.

2. **Human Labor (The Input of Energy)**

   - **Hourly Wages:** For a standardized set of jobs (e.g., retail worker, cashier, manual laborer) at a local level.
   - **Gig Economy Rates:** Average pay for common tasks (food delivery, parcel delivery).

3. **Core Commodities (The Foundational Layer)**
   - **Precious Metals:** Gold, Silver.
   - **Industrial & Energy:** Copper, Lithium, Oil, Natural Gas.
   - **Agricultural:** Wheat, Corn, Soybeans.

---

## State & Notation

- S_t — SZX supply.
- q*{i,t}, p*{i,t} — reserve quantity & price of asset i \in \mathcal{C}.
- **Reserve value**: R*t=\sum_i q*{i,t}\,p\_{i,t}.
- **Collateralization ratio**: \mathrm{CR}\_t = \frac{R_t}{S_t}.
- **Target CR**: \(\mathrm{CR}^\*\) (e.g., 130–200% depending on risk).
- **Market price** (DEX TWAP): P^{\text{mkt}}\_t.
- **Target Redemption Price**: \mathrm{TRP}\_t \approx 1.
- **Price error (log-space)**: e_t = \ln P^{\text{mkt}}\_t - \ln \mathrm{TRP}\_t.
- **Volatility**: \sigma_t (recent realized vol of P^{\text{mkt}}).

## Supply Logic

### Supply Hard Cap

```
MAX_SUPPLY = α × Global_Human_Population
```

### Minting & Burning

```
Minted_SZX = Collateral_Value / DSAVI
Burned_SZX = DSAVI / Collateral_Value
```

Collateralized assets include:

- ZEC (shielded in Zcash L1)
- BTC
- ETH / LSTs (via EVM integration)

---

# The Sozu Oracle Network: A Deep Dive into the "Sensory Cortex" of Real-World Value

The goal is not to create _another_ price feed for DeFi. The goal is to create a **decentralized, Sybil-resistant, and cryptographically secure consensus mechanism for the cost of human life and labor itself.**

## Oracle Architecture: A Multi-Layered, Decentralized Nervous System

This isn't one monolithic oracle. It's a network of specialized oracles feeding into a master consensus layer.

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                          APPLICATION LAYER                            |
|      (Wallets, Merchants, DApps using the SZX Token)                  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
                              | (Queries Finalized Value)
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                       CONSENSUS & AGGREGATION LAYER                   |
|  +-----------------+  +-----------------+  +-----------------+        |
|  | Regional Index  |  | Regional Index  |  | Global Index    |        |
|  | (e.g., LATAM)   |  | (e.g., SE Asia) |  | (Commodities)   |        |
|  +-----------------+  +-----------------+  +-----------------+        |
|         | Data              | Data                 | Data             |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
                              | (Submits Verified Data)
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                         VALIDATION & INCENTIVE LAYER                  |
|  +-----------------+  +-----------------+  +-----------------+        |
|  |  Data Curators  |  |  Staked Nodes   |  | Dispute/Arb     |        |
|  |  (Human Oracles)|  |  (Algorithmic   |  |   System        |        |
|  |                 |  |   Validation)   |  |                 |        |
|  +-----------------+  +-----------------+  +-----------------+        |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
                              | (Raw Data Submission)
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                          DATA SOURCE LAYER                            |
|  +-----------------+  +-----------------+  +-----------------+        |
|  |  Mobile App     |  |  API Feeds      |  |  Physical       |        |
|  |  (Photo + GPS)  |  |  (TradFi Ind.)  |  |  QR/NFC Tags    |        |
|  +-----------------+  +-----------------+  +-----------------+        |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### **Layer 1: Data Source Layer**

- **Human Oracles (Crowdsourced):** The soul of the network. They use a dedicated Sozu app to:
  - **Geotag:** Every submission is tied to a GPS location.
  - **Timestamp:** Precise time of observation.
  - **Visual Proof:** Upload a photo of the price tag/shelf/receipt.
  - **Category Tagging:** Classify the item (e.g., "Banana," "1L Gasoline").
- **API Feeds (Bootstrap & Cross-Reference):** Initially, we pull from established TradFi indexes (CPI, BLS, FAO Food Price Index) and commodity exchanges (COMEX, LBMA) to bootstrap and provide a baseline for consensus.
- **Physical World Integration:** Partner with merchants to place QR/NFC tags on shelves that automatically report prices to the network when scanned.

### **Layer 2: Validation & Incentive Layer (The "Trust Engine")**

This is where the magic happens. We need to prevent Sybil attacks and spam.

- **Staked Node Network:** Nodes must stake SZX tokens to participate in validation. Their role is to:
  1. **Cluster Submissions:** Group reports by location, time, and item.
  2. **Run Consensus Algorithms:** Calculate the median price for a cluster. Reports that fall within a certain standard deviation are considered "truthful."
  3. **Slash/ Reward:** Nodes are rewarded for honest validation. They can also vote to slash the stake of a node that acts maliciously or is consistently offline.
- **Oracle Reputation System:** Each human oracle has a reputation score.
  - **New Users:** Start with a low reputation and a low earning cap.
  - **Accurate Reports:** Submissions that are consistently near the consensus median _increase_ reputation and earning potential.
  - **Outlier Reports:** Submissions consistently far from the median _decrease_ reputation.
  - **Collusion Detection:** Algorithms detect patterns of coordinated false reporting (e.g., 100 new accounts in one location all reporting the same wrong price) and flag them for review.
- **Dispute Resolution:** A decentralized court system (like Kleros or Aragon) can be used to adjudicate disputes over slashing or data validity.

### **Layer 3: Consensus & Aggregation Layer**

- **Regional Price Feeds:** The validated data is aggregated into regional indexes (e.g., "Cost of 1kg Rice in Southeast Asia," "Average Hourly Wage for Retail in the Eurozone"). This respects local economic realities.
- **Global Commodity Index:** A separate, purely global index for things like Gold and Oil.
- **The Acquisitive Power Index (API):** This is the master formula. It's a weighted basket that combines:
  `API = (K1 * Regional Essential Basket) + (K2 * Regional Labor Index) + (K3 * Global Commodity Index)`
  Where `K1, K2, K3` are weights that can be governed by the SZX community.

## The Tokenomics of Truth: Incentivizing Honest Reporting

This is the flywheel that makes the system work.

- **Mint-to-Earn:** A portion of the SZX token supply is minted daily to reward oracles and validators.
- **Payment for Accuracy:** Rewards are distributed based on:
  1. **Reputation Score:** Higher score = higher share of the reward pool.
  2. **Data Scarcity:** Reporting from data-sparse regions (e.g., rural Africa) is rewarded more highly than reporting from Manhattan, to encourage global coverage.
  3. **Economic Significance:** Reporting on a core item like "1kg of rice" is worth more than reporting on "a branded soft drink."
- **Cost of Dishonesty:** Losing staked tokens (for nodes) or reputation (for human oracles) makes attacks economically non-viable.

---

# Algorithmic Stability: The TRP Controller & Arbitrage Mechanism

## Peg Logic: Controller & TRP

Use a conservative controller so TRP stays very close to $1 but can creep if needed (e.g., market stress recovery):

```
ln TRP_{t+1} = ln TRP_t - k_p e_t - k_i ∑_{τ=t-H}^{t} e_τ - k_d (e_t - e_{t-1})
```

- Small k's → slow, robust adjustments; default TRP → 1.0000.
- Controller runs per-epoch (e.g., hourly) to avoid twitchiness.

## Mint / Redeem Arbitrage (Main Loop)

**Mint (when P^{mkt}\_t > TRP_t)**

- Arbitrageur deposits a **basket** worth TRP_t per SZX (weighted by w_i) into reserve; receives newly minted SZX.
- Sells SZX on the market toward P^{mkt}\_t ↓ TRP_t.
- **Profit per token** (ignoring slippage):

```
Π_mint ≈ (P^{mkt}_t - TRP_t) - f_mint
```

**Redeem (when P^{mkt}\_t < TRP_t)**

- Arbitrageur buys SZX cheaper, redeems at TRP for basket; SZX is **burned**.
- **Profit per token**:

```
Π_redeem ≈ (TRP_t - P^{mkt}_t) - f_redeem
```

**Throughput caps** T^{mint}\_t, T^{redeem}\_t limit per-epoch flow to avoid reserve thrash:

```
T^{redeem}_t ∝ max(0, CR_t - CR_min)
T^{mint}_t ∝ max(0, CR_max - CR_t)
```

## Fees & Incentives

### Stability Fee on Outstanding SZX

A drifting "interest" (can be 0 or even negative during stress) that nudges CR toward target and prices risk:

```
SF_t = b_0 + α max(0, CR* - CR_t) + β σ_t
```

Accrues to **Surplus Buffer** \mathcal{B} and/or **SZS stakers**.

### Mint/Redeem Fees (dynamic)

Raise fees when volatility or redemptions spike; lower them for tight spreads:

```
f_{mint,redeem},t = f_0 + c_1 |e_t| + c_2 σ_t + c_3 utilization_t
```

### Surplus Usage

If buffer exceeds threshold and CR_t ≥ CR\*, protocol **buys SZX on DEX and burns** → supports peg and reduces supply:

```
ΔS_t^{buyback} = (B_t - B^{min}) / P^{mkt}_t
```

## Reserve Management & CR Dynamics

**Reserve value**

```
R_t = ∑_i q_{i,t} p_{i,t} ⇒ CR_t = R_t / S_t
```

**Targeted weighting** solves:

```
min_{w_i} Var(∑_i w_i r_i) s.t. ∑_i w_i = 1, w_i ∈ [0,c_i], liquidity/risk caps
```

Periodic rebalancing trades between reserve assets to minimize variance and tail risk while preserving on-chain liquidity.

**Drawdown handling:** if CR_t falls:

- **Raise SF** and **mint/redeem fees** (slows redemptions).
- Sell **SZS** (junior) via Dutch auction for reserve assets (recap).
- If threshold breached, **temporary redeem throttles** kick in (rate limit, auction-based exits).

## Tranching & Loss Absorption

- **Senior (SZX)** — claims on reserve at TRP; protected until buffers deplete.
- **Junior (SZS)** — earns fees & upside; **first-loss** in reserve drawdowns.
- **Insurance Vault** — optional pool staked by SZS holders; pays out on stress in exchange for higher fee share.

Loss waterfall:

```
Loss ⇒ B (surplus) → Insurance Vault → SZS value → (last) redeem throttles
```

---

# Zcash Strategic Integration

## "Zcash as Digital Gold, SZX as Stable Private Money"

**Zcash** acts as a shielded, auditable reserve for minting SZX — enabling:

- Full privacy-preserving collateral layer
- On-chain proof of reserves via zero-knowledge bridges
- Cross-chain transaction privacy

### Cross-Chain Reserve Architecture:

```
[SZX Token] ←→ [Sozu Contracts (Noir, Solidity)] ←→ [ZEC Pool (Zcash L1)]
```

### ZEC Mint Logic (Pseudocode)

```rust
contract ZcashReserve {
    #[storage]
    struct Storage {
        shielded_zec_reserves: PrivateState<Field>,
        bridge_verifier: PublicState<Field>,
        collateral_ratio: PublicState<Field>
    }

    #[private]
    fn mint_szx_from_zec(zec_proof: Field, amount: Field) -> Field {
        assert(verify_zcash_bridge(zec_proof) == 1);
        let current_reserves = storage.shielded_zec_reserves.read();
        storage.shielded_zec_reserves.write(current_reserves + amount);
        let szx_to_mint = calculate_mint_amount(amount);
        return szx_to_mint;
    }
}
```

---

# The Phased Deployment: From Fiat-Peg to Reality-Peg

**Phase 1: The Fiat-Anchored Bootstrap (SZX v1)**

- **Goal:** Establish liquidity and user trust.
- **Mechanism:** SZX is pegged to a basket of high-quality, decentralized fiat stablecoins (USDC, DAI, etc.).
- **Oracle Role:** _Minimal._ The oracle merely tracks the value of this basket. This is the training wheels phase.

**Phase 2: The Hybrid Index (SZX v2)**

- **Goal:** Introduce the real-world index while maintaining stability.
- **Mechanism:** The peg becomes a weighted average between the Fiat Basket and the new Acquisitive Power Index (API).
  - `SZX_Value = (W1 * FiatBasket) + (W2 * API)`
  - Initially, `W1` is high (e.g., 0.8) and `W2` is low (e.g., 0.2).
- **Oracle Role:** _Critical._ The network is live and being tested. Over time, through governance, `W1` is decreased and `W2` is increased.

**Phase 3: The Full Depeg (SZX v3)**

- **Goal:** Achieve monetary sovereignty based on real-world value.
- **Mechanism:** `W1` is reduced to 0. The value of 1 SZX is defined solely by the Acquisitive Power Index.
  `1 SZX = 1 Unit of Global Acquisitive Power`
- **Oracle Role:** _The Foundation._ The entire monetary system now rests on the security and accuracy of the Sozu Oracle Network. It has become the planet's decentralized price discovery mechanism.

---

# Sozu Pay – Merchant Interface

## Key Features:

- One-click SZX payment link (Mercadopago / Stripe style)
- Instant stable payments (no volatility)
- Optional fiat conversion through internal zkp2p
- Auto-yield accrual for merchants

## Sozu Pay Stack:

- Wallet SDK (Web3 + Privacy UX)
- Transaction explorer with pseudonymity
- Embedded checkout widget
- Fee-sharing for staking SZX

---

# Privacy Layer

Zcash's zero-knowledge capabilities anchor privacy across all layers:

- Mint/redeem with shielded ZEC
- In-pool transfers with zero-knowledge balances
- Optional view keys for audits

## Privacy Mode (Optional Layer)

- **Transfers**: shielded UTXO-like notes or stealth addresses; note commitments live in a privacy pool.
- **Bridges**: mint/redeem boundaries remain public (for reserve accounting), while **in-pool transfers** are private.
- **View keys**: optional user-held disclosure for audits or compliance when _the user_ opts in.

_(Economics above remain identical whether shielded or transparent.)_

---

# Oracles & Market Plumbing

- **Prices**: Medianized on-chain DEX TWAP + pull-based oracle (e.g., Chainlink style) with sanity bounds.
- **Circuit breakers**: freeze controller updates if oracle divergence > δ or data stale > T_max.
- **Auction venues**: All recapitalizations and rebalances are public, batched, and MEV-minimized.

---

# Stress Scenarios & Responses

1. **Market price** < **TRP (sell-pressure)**
   - Arbitrage **buy → redeem** burns supply.
   - **Redeem fee** up, **throughput cap** enforces paced exits.
   - **SF** rises, surplus accumulates; SZS auctions if CR approaches floor.
2. **Market price** > **TRP (buy-pressure)**
   - Arbitrage **mint → sell** grows supply.
   - **Mint fee** increases to avoid overshoot; **CR** guided toward CR\*.
3. **Oracle failure / extreme vol**
   - Freeze TRP updates; widen fees; cap mint/redeem; switch to auction-based settlement until data normalizes.
4. **Reserve drawdown**
   - Automatic SZS auctions; Insurance Vault taps; redeem rate limits.
   - Controller can **nudge TRP** slowly (<10 bps/day) to assist orderly recap if needed.

---

# Yield & Governance

### Staking Yield:

- 15–20% APY from Sozu Pay transaction fees
- Lock durations increase multiplier
- Collateral staking eligibility for mint rights

### Governance:

- On-chain Noir voting mechanism
- DSAVI basket weights, oracle rules, and inflation curves governed by SZX holders

---

# Minimal Equations Summary

- Reserve & CR: R*t = ∑_i q*{i,t} p\_{i,t}, CR_t = R_t/S_t
- Controller: ln TRP\_{t+1} = ln TRP_t - k_p e_t - k_i∑e - k_d Δe
- Arbitrage profits:
  - Π_mint ≈ (P^{mkt} - TRP) - f_mint
  - Π_redeem ≈ (TRP - P^{mkt}) - f_redeem
- Stability fee: SF_t = b_0 + α(CR\* - CR_t)^+ + β σ_t
- Buyback burn: ΔS^{buyback} = (B_t - B^{min})/P^{mkt}\_t

---

# Parameter Sketch (starting points)

- CR\* = 1.5 (150%); CR_min = 1.2; CR_max = 2.0
- Controller k_p = 0.05, k_i = 0.01, k_d = 0.02; epoch = 1h
- Fees baseline f_0 = 5 bps; bounds 0–40 bps; utilization-linked
- Redeem/mint throughput caps: 1–3% of supply per epoch (adaptive to CR and vol)
- Surplus min B^{min}: 1–2% of R_t

---

# Implementation Roadmap

### Phase 1 – MVP (Now)

- SZX EVM contracts (NoirLang)
- Oracle testnet submissions
- Sozu Pay v0.1 prototype
- Initial ZEC reserve bridge test

### Phase 2 – Privacy & Rebase

- Shielded balance rebasing logic
- DSAVI index public UI + data
- Sozu Pay merchant beta onboarding

### Phase 3 – Full Protocol Launch

- Bridge to Zcash mainnet
- Full DAO transition
- Foundation & public GitHub repo

---

# Investment Ask: $8,000

Retroactive fund for Research and development of the whitepaper, will be used to continue research before deploying the first version of SozuPay.

- Launch Sozu Pay merchant pilot (Chile/Argentina)
- Publish documentation

---

# Final Statement

**Sozu Cash is not a speculative asset. It's a public monetary tool.**

**Built with Zcash. Extended through Ethereum. Governed by users.**

> Wealth measured in life, not fiat.

**SZX is not a financial product, but a protocolized measure of decentralized value — a successor to fiat money, not an imitation of it.**

The SZX token becomes the representation of this stability. It's not a "stablecoin"; it's the first **Realitycoin** — dynamically stable because it's constantly adjusting to the waves of human economic activity. It's not pegged to a dying paradigm (fiat), but to the living, breathing reality of what it costs to be a human on this planet.

This is the blueprint. The next step is to define the initial basket weights, the specific consensus algorithms (e.g., Schelling point games), and the tokenomic parameters for the mint-to-earn model.


### Time Period of Work Completion

Q4 2025- Q4 2025

### Total Budget (USD)

8000

### Budget Breakdown

This request represents a retroactive investment in the foundational research and high-level systems architecture that has produced a compelling vision for a Zcash-native stable value protocol. The amount is calculated based on the significant, specialized R&D effort required to create a technically sound and ecosystem-aligned design.

Below is the detailed justification:

- Compensation:

$(USD): $5,600

Justification: This covers the core intellectual labor of architectural design and technical writing.

Architectural Research & Design (80 hours @ $70/hr): This involved not just understanding Zcash's infrastructure (ZK-proofs, shielded pools) but creatively designing a novel system (DSAVI, Noir integration, ZEC-as-reserve) that leverages it. The $70/hour rate is competitive for a senior blockchain architect specializing in cryptography and economic mechanisms.

Whitepaper Drafting & Technical Documentation (40 hours @ $70/hr): Translating complex architectural concepts into a clear, persuasive, and technically precise document for the Zcash community requires skilled technical writing.

- Technology/Software:

$(USD): $1,200

Justification: Costs associated with the development and testing environment.

Noir Language Tooling & Development Suite: Subscription and access fees for specialized IDE plugins, proving backends (e.g., Barretenberg), and simulation environments necessary to prototype and validate the contract logic outlined in the whitepaper.

Software Licenses: Access to professional-grade design, diagramming, and collaborative coding software used to produce the architecture diagrams and smart contract pseudocode.

- Services/Contractors:

$(USD): $1,200

Justification: Targeted expert review to ensure quality and alignment.

Specialized Cryptographic Review ($500): A one-time consultation with a ZK-proof expert to review the proposed integration of Noir with Zcash's proving system, ensuring the architectural soundness of our cross-chain proof model.

Economic Mechanism Design Review ($500): A review by a token economist to stress-test the DSAVI model and the ZEC collateral mechanism, ensuring its stability and incentive compatibility before public release.

- Total $(USD): $8,000

our goal is to Increase ZEC Utility: By positioning it as a primary reserve asset.

Drive On-Chain Activity: Through a new class of private DeFi transactions.

Strengthen Zcash's Narrative: By providing a flagship use-case for its privacy technology.

## Project Summary

In December of 2024, slow sync was a critical usability issue blocking Zcash adoption.

As described below, and [posted on the Zcash Forums](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/pepper-sync/52445) Zingo Labs produced a novel sync implementation that's competitive with the fastest alternatives in raw performance, and was the fastest spend-before-sync implementation in production when it was completed.

In addition to the direct benefit to the community provided by a new sync implementation, there has been a salutary effect on other sync providers.

---

## Project Description

To ensure complete transaction privacy, decryption operations that might reveal sensitive information must take place on the recipient's device.

Since it's often desirable to transact using a limited-resource mobile device, this means that a high volume (all transactions on chain) of computationally intensive (attempted, aka "trial," decryption) operations are necessarily performed on these devices.

Colloquially we refer to this as **"The Syncing Problem."**

We used ideas from DAG Sync, and primitives from lower layer libraries (incremental merkle tree), to solve the problem efficiently.

---

## Technical Approach

##### Pepper-Sync, Incremental Merkle Tree

Zcash uses merkle trees to efficiently prove that a given element (value commitment) is in a set (the set of receipts).

If a value-commitment is revealed to belong to a particular recipient (upon trial-decryption), then the recipient learns that they must be able to construct a path to the root of the tree to prove the commitment (the recipient's source of funds) is in the set of receipts (funding sources).  
If, on the other hand, the value-commitment does not belong to the recipient, then the recipient learns about a path that it does not need to compute.  
As the recipient marks more commitments as relevant to it, or not, it can determine a minimal tree that is necessary to compute all paths to its receipts.

`pepper-sync` uses the incremental merkle tree Rust package to avoid unnecessary computation.

##### Pepper-Sync, Nullifier Lookup

Because successful decryption of a transaction allows computation of the corresponding nullifier (which can be used to subsequently prove the transaction output is spent), and because change receipts are among the outputs of standard transactions (that have change), and because nullifiers are not encrypted on chain, `pepper-sync` uses nullifier lookup to non-linearly track receipts of funds spent from previously detected transactions.  

This is quite useful for older receipts as it allows the detection of relevant outputs that might be generated much later in time (and outputs/blocks) permitting recipients access to the funds long before a linear scan could do so.

##### Pepper-Sync, Prioritized Scanning

These innovations coupled with prioritization primitives from `librustzcash` and a clean and idiomatic Rust implementation of multithreaded sync are the core of **pepper-sync**.

##### Supporting Context, End-User Access to Pepper-Sync

The following work was carried out in parallel to the core implementation, and was necessary to enable end-Users to benefit from work on the core algorithm.

- In-person activities: 5+ events in collaboration with Zcash en Español and ZK-Radio, including participation in Aleph-Crecimiento (Argentina).
- Social media management: 80% growth in followers, with active presence on X, Instagram, Bluesky, Free2Z, Discord and Telegram.
- Articles on Free2Z: 15+ publications covering updates, features, and characteristics of ZingoLabs products.
- Graphic design: 500+ visual assets created to promote activities, events, and updates across multiple platforms.
- Support: continuous assistance provided to users on the use and configuration of ZingoLabs tools, as well as guidance in reporting bugs and identifying possible solutions.
- Technological impact: growth in total downloads from 4.1K to 6.5K on Android and from 3K to 4.6K on iOS.

**Compensation:** $345,600  * ~6x (increase in value ZEC/USD) = $1,975,000.00
**Justification:** 2 full-time developers for 9 months at $120/hour.

This cost to Zingo Labs was calculated using the price of ZEC in USD during the period of work. Our ask is scaled to reflect the current (low) price of ZEC ~ $250USD/ZEC.

We assumed an hourly rate of $120 and estimated 2 full time developers were allocated for the duration.

The price of ZEC for the duration was estimated to reach a maximum price in USD of less $60, with most estimates of the average in the $40 - $50 range.   This gives the conservative scaling factor of ~5.7.

At current prices, (which will almost certainly seem absurdly low very soon), this ask represents about 10% of the funds that will be available in the lockbox at disbursement.

Zingo Labs intends to apply for ZCG funding to improve `pepper-sync` and build new applications on top of it.

---

## Success Metrics

Because `pepper-sync` supported out-of-order sync and spend-before-sync, it allowed funds discovered deep in the chain to be efficiently spent even if most of the chain was not yet trial decrypted.  
This innovation is critical to support the effective use of long-ZODL’d funds.

Its raw performance is rapidly approaching `warp-sync`'s which now is approximately 2x faster in certain scenarios, but leverages different mechanisms to achieve throughput.

This means that potential synergies that use innovations from both sync engines should be able to achieve another boost in performance. It also opens the possibility of competitive efforts in sync performance which will benefit consumers.

- `zexcavator` is known to have recovered buried funds, and *if funded* will be upgraded to handle sweeping up multi-sapling-spend-key funds, to discover and spend zecwallet-generated transactions.

To do so it will leverage the unique spend-before-sync implementation of `pepper-sync`.

We upgraded and expanded Zcash support in Unstoppable Wallet — enabling users to view both shielded (z-address) and unshielded (t-address) balances, perform one-tap shielding and benefit from improved performance and security through the latest Zcash SDK integration.

### Project Description

Between versions 0.41.0 -> 0.45.0, Unstoppable Wallet implemented a series of deep upgrades to its Zcash integration, enhancing usability, privacy, and SDK compatibility.

These upgrades brought Zcash support to a mature and stable level within Unstoppable Wallet, ensuring secure and reliable handling of shielded transactions.
Users can now:
- Instantly view both shielded and unshielded balances in a single unified interface.
- Convert (shield) unshielded funds with one tap, directly within the wallet UI.
- Benefit from the latest Zcash SDK (improved sync, memo handling, transaction reliability).
- Experience significantly faster performance for balance loading and transaction verification.

All changes are open-source and verified via our public GitHub repository.
This work substantially improved Zcash’s visibility among privacy-focused users, increasing shielded transaction activity and overall exposure to the ZEC ecosystem.

### Technical Approach (how you did it)

The updates involved a combination of SDK upgrades, UX engineering, and privacy optimizations:

**Zcash SDK Upgrade**
- Migrated to the latest ECC Zcash SDK.
- Refactored wallet synchronization and memo management for shielded transactions.
- Verified compatibility with lightwalletd nodes and improved performance benchmarks.

**Unified Balance View**
- Implemented logic to aggregate shielded and transparent balances under one account.
- Designed a “Privacy Level” indicator showing which funds are shielded.

**One-Tap Shielding UX**
- Introduced a simplified flow for shielding t-address coins in one tap.
- Added background shielding notifications and progress indicators.

**Enhanced Security & Testing**
- Conducted regression tests for Zcash transaction handling and memo encryption.
- Validated transactions through multiple lightwalletd servers.
- Audited SDK upgrade impact on performance and battery usage.

These improvements were deployed through production releases 0.41.0, 0.43.0, and 0.45.0 on GitHub.

Q4 2024 – Q4 2025

All completed work will be verified and accepted by its intended users or their representatives, who will confirm that the outputs meet the required quality, functionality, and usability before the work is listed as an option for Coinholder voting.

- [x] I understand when contributing to existing Zcash code, I am required to adhere to the project specific contribution guidelines, paying close attention to any [merge](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#merge-workflow), [branch](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#branch-history), [pull request](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-review), and [commit](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages) guidelines as exemplified in the librustzcash repository.
- [x] I understand all grants are valued in USD but will be disbursed in Shielded ZEC. I acknowledge and accept that disbursement amounts may fluctuate based on the ZEC/USD exchange rate at the time of payment.

### Application Owners

@Tomas-M

### Organization or Individual Name

Tomas Matejicek

### Additional Team Members

```team-members.yaml
None
```

### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

Zcash community forum

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

800000

### Category

Non-Wallet Applications

### Project Summary

CrowdStore is a browser-based, fully decentralized P2P marketplace and store network, which lets anyone run stores without servers, with orders and ratings encrypted in Zcash memo fields and data shared among peers. Anonymous, signature-verified trades and post-order rating create trust and transparency while showcasing Zcash’s privacy tech. **CrowdStore completes the Zcash ecosystem by giving users a practical way to earn and spend Zcash.**

### Project Description

CrowdStore.net is an anonymous, browser-based peer-to-peer marketplace designed to redefine online commerce through decentralization and privacy. The marketplace itself, including stores, admins, and buyers, operates fully decentralized without centralized servers or intermediaries, allowing users to create, host, and operate online stores directly from their browsers. All store data is distributed among connected peers via WebRTC, ensuring resilience, autonomy, and censorship resistance. Transactions are conducted exclusively in Zcash, leveraging its encrypted memo fields to securely store order details, ratings, and other sensitive information.

The project’s core goal is to empower users with a secure, private, and decentralized alternative to traditional e-commerce platforms, which are often burdened by surveillance, data collection, and high fees. By integrating cryptographic signatures, a reputation system, and an automated escrow mechanism coordinated through a distributed Payment Service Provider (PSP), CrowdStore.net ensures authenticity, trust, and fairness without sacrificing user anonymity.

Through this approach, the platform demonstrates how Zcash can serve as the foundation for a practical, real-world privacy-preserving economy. CrowdStore.net not only promotes Zcash adoption but also advances the broader mission of user sovereignty, giving individuals full control over their data, transactions, and digital businesses.

How it works in practice:
- Merchants create their stores, add items, define shipping rules, and publish their unique StoreID. 
- The StoreID is also a public key which verifies everything.
- Buyers access a store using this StoreID, connecting to other peers who have the same store data rather than directly to the merchant. 
- Ordered items and delivery address are embedded in Zcash transactions, with all details securely stored in the encrypted memo field during payment. 
- The Payment Service Provider (PSP) coordinates payment and escrow, releasing funds once delivery is confirmed. 
- After receiving the product, the buyer can issue a signed rating to finalize the transaction, rating is stored and calculated at PSP level

Payment coordination: CrowdStore operates entirely in the browser with a fully decentralized peer-to-peer marketplace architecture, while payment processing and escrow functions are handled through the companion distributed Payment Service Provider (PSP). The PSP is a separate, independently deployed component that interfaces with the Zcash network to manage holds, releases, refunds, and related payment logic. Advanced users may choose to replace the PSP with a custom or self-hosted system.

### Technical Approach (how you did it)

The decentralized marketplace is implemented entirely in client-side HTML and JavaScript with native WebRTC for peer connections - no frameworks. Store catalogs and listings are authored and signed in the browser, then shared over WebRTC DataChannels among connected peers. All sensitive payloads that may traverse the network or be embedded in Zcash transactions are encrypted client-side using the browser’s SubtleCrypto API (elliptic-curve primitives for signing; AES for confidential data). Ratings and order confirmations are produced as signed messages so any peer can verify integrity.

Payments and escrow are handled by a separately deployed, distributed Payment Service Provider (PSP) I developed as a companion project. The PSP acts as a bridge between WebRTC and Zcash. It connects to the Zcash network via a light wallet backend (currently using zinolib/zingo-cli), which I contributed patches to in order to improve automation and reliability for programmatic use; these changes were accepted upstream. The PSP orchestrates holds, releases, refunds, and ratings, while never accessing buyer-only private data; delivery details always remain end-to-end encrypted and packed into Zcash memo fields.

To maximize the limited capacity of Zcash memo fields, I created **BPEZip**, a small open-source compression library tailored for short texts. It achieves roughly 20-40% size reduction on typical order payloads and is integrated into the client: data is compressed, then encrypted, then embedded in memos. This significantly expands what can be stored privately on-chain without altering the payment UX.

Peer distribution runs directly on WebRTC DataChannels. Catalogs and store metadata are cached ephemerally by connected browsers to improve availability while peers are online. For persistence and smoother discovery, an auxiliary service can opportunistically keep selected stores available when origin peers are offline, and community-run nodes can do the same; this layer is minimal and does not alter the trust model because content remains signed and verifiable end-to-end.

Deployment is intentionally simple. A dedicated server hosts the public entry point and documentation, but the marketplace also ships as a downloadable HTML/JS package that runs from local files via the file:// protocol - no local web server required. This keeps distribution flexible and censorship-resistant.

A lightweight signaling server is required solely for establishing WebRTC connections between peers. It performs the initial exchange of connection metadata such as ICE candidates and session descriptions, enabling browsers to discover and connect directly to one another. The signaling server does not store or process any user data, store content, or transaction information - it functions purely as a transient relay during peer connection setup. Once peers are connected, all communication, data exchange, and encryption occur directly between browsers without involving the signaling server.

Development began with an initial proof of concept roughly a decade ago and matured into the current codebase built during 2024–2025. Over these two years I iterated on the browser-native crypto, integrated the PSP and light-wallet flows, implemented the WebRTC data layer, added BPEZip, and stabilized end-to-end signing and verification. I also designed and implemented the entire user interface and frontend visuals, focusing on usability and clarity for both technical and non-technical users. This includes the main website with documentation and onboarding pages, the admin section for managing stores and transactions, and the store section for sellers and buyers to interact securely and intuitively. The result is a production-ready, browser-only marketplace that demonstrates practical, privacy-preserving commerce using Zcash.

Here is a list of things I did

* Designed and implemented a fully client-side marketplace using only native HTML, JavaScript, and WebRTC (no frameworks).
* Built browser-based authoring and signing for store catalogs and listings using SubtleCrypto elliptic-curve primitives.
* Implemented end-to-end encryption for all sensitive data with AES for confidentiality and ECDSA for signing and verification.
* Established peer-to-peer data exchange via WebRTC DataChannels, enabling catalog and listing sharing directly between browsers.
* Integrated the PSP for payments and rating.
* Designed secure packing of encrypted delivery details into Zcash memo fields for private on-chain storage.
* Implemented **BPEZip**, a custom compression library for short texts, reducing memo payload sizes by 20–40%.
* Integrated compression + encryption workflow in the client before embedding order data into Zcash transactions.
* Implemented a minimal WebRTC signaling server to relay ICE candidates and session descriptions for peer discovery.
* Created a simple deployment model with a static entry server and downloadable HTML/JS package runnable via `file://` protocol.
* Designed and implemented the full user interface: marketplace front-end, admin tools, store management, and onboarding flows.
* Focused UI/UX design on clarity and usability for both technical and non-technical users.
* Delivered a working proof-of-concept evolved into a production-ready, privacy-preserving Zcash-integrated marketplace.


### Time Period of Work Completion

2024-2025

### Total Budget (USD)

800000

### Budget Breakdown

- Compensation: 800000 USD
   - Justification: Full-time compensation for Tomas Matejicek as the sole developer, designer, and project manager over multiple years of development. This covers architecture design, frontend implementation for store owners (admin section) and buyers (storefront for end users), WebRTC networking, Zcash integration via the light-wallet interface, PSP integration, cryptographic functionality, UI/UX design, documentation, and long-term maintenance. The budget reflects the scope of a complete, production-grade decentralized platform built independently with sustained effort, released publicly under MIT license.

- Total $(USD): 800000

Note: A significant portion of the requested compensation is not intended for direct personal enrichment. Rather, it will be strategically reinvested into comprehensive advertising initiatives and community engagement efforts designed to enhance awareness and participation - thereby generating future revenue streams that will, finally, be allocated toward personal enrichment :-). This sustainable model is expected to attract new participants to the Zcash ecosystem, support wallet integrations, and increase shielded on-chain transaction volume, positioning CrowdStore.net as the practical conduit between Zcash’s technical potential and mainstream, privacy-oriented commerce.

### Previous Funding

No

### Previous Funding Details

_No response_

### Other Funding Sources

No

### Other Funding Sources Details

_No response_

### Success Metrics

The project brings direct, tangible value to the Zcash community by providing a fully functional real-world use case for shielded Zcash payments. Until now, Zcash’s privacy technology has primarily been used for transfers and savings; CrowdStore.net extends its purpose into practical, everyday commerce. It introduces a live, fully decentralized marketplace, where every transaction, rating, and order detail uses encrypted Zcash memo fields, with payments and ratings coordinated through a distributed PSP layer, demonstrating the full potential of private payments in real-world applications.

Quantitatively, success is measured through user adoption and transaction volume: the number of unique stores created, total shielded Zcash transactions processed through the marketplace, and the rate of returning buyers and sellers. Additionally, engagement metrics such as peer connection counts, uptime of distributed store data, and the number of ratings submitted reflect healthy ecosystem activity. Since the project is new, these metrics are to be determined in the future.

Qualitatively, the project delivers an essential proof of concept for how Zcash can power privacy-respecting economic systems. It validates Zcash as a platform for anonymous, censorship-resistant trade, not only as a currency but as the foundation for decentralized business infrastructure.

### Proof of completion

- Repository/Commit:
  - github repository is private. Access will be granted to selected reviewers upon request
- Deployment/Release:
  - main website https://crowdstore.net
  - documentation  https://crowdstore.net/learn-more.html
  - example working store: https://crowdstore.net/#simps43dTPDxWQeVNREH4tYY5gpHzJ2GpQeteSAb2M7T
  - create new store: https://crowdstore.net/admin/index.html#create

### Conflict of Interest Disclosure

There are no actual, potential, or perceived conflicts of interest related to this application. I, Tomas Matejicek, am the sole developer and creator of the CrowdStore.net project and its associated components, including the Payment Service Provider (PSP) and the BPEZip compression library. All work was conceived, designed, and implemented independently.

### Terms and Conditions

All completed work will be verified and accepted by its intended users or their representatives, who will confirm that the outputs meet the required quality, functionality, and usability before the work is listed as an option for Coinholder voting.
- [x] I agree that for any new open-source software, I will create a CONTRIBUTING.md file that reflects the high standards of Zcash development, using the [`librustzcash` style guides](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#styleguides) as a primary reference.
- [x] I understand when contributing to existing Zcash code, I am required to adhere to the project specific contribution guidelines, paying close attention to any [merge](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#merge-workflow), [branch](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#branch-history), [pull request](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-review), and [commit](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit-messages) guidelines as exemplified in the librustzcash repository.
- [x] I understand all grants are valued in USD but will be disbursed in Shielded ZEC. I acknowledge and accept that disbursement amounts may fluctuate based on the ZEC/USD exchange rate at the time of payment.

### Application Owners (@octocat, @octocat1)

@BTCxEagle

### Organization or Individual Name

BitcoinVN

### Additional Team Members

```team-members.yaml
CTO - Alex Winter ( https://packagist.org/packages/bitcoinvn/bitcoinvn-php )
```

### How did you learn about the Lockbox: Coinholder Retroactive Grants Program?

Direct conversation with Zcash ecosystem participants

### Requested Grant Amount (USD)

10000

### Category

Infrastructure

### Project Summary

BitcoinVN has been operating in Vietnam as its premier Bitcoin Exchange service provider since 2014 ( https://bitcoinvn.io/news/how-can-i-trust-bitcoinvn/ ).

Over the years, the service has expanded to provide a no-sign-up instant cryptocurrency swap functionality.

Furthermore, the team operates physical infrastructure such as Vietnam's largest BTM network ( https://bitcoinvn.io/btm ) and provides tools & services to make self-custody easier accessible for their customer base ( https://bitcoinvn.io/shop/ ).

### Project Description

BitcoinVN has finalized and successfully integrated shielded Zcash (ZEC) swaps on its instant swap platform:

https://bitcoinvn.io/?deposit=usdt&settle=zecshielded

https://bitcoinvn.io/?deposit=zecshielded&settle=btc

API integration into other services is possible via:

https://bitcoinvn.io/api/doc

One of our prior updates regarding Zcash can be found here:

https://bitcoinvn.io/news/zcash-infrastructure-upgrades/

Furthermore, as an add-on, we successfully integrated shielded Zcash (ZEC) as payment method into our online shop:

https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/bitcoinvn-zec-infrastructure-upgrade-q3-2025/52092/2

### Technical Approach (how you did it)

We had previously successfully integrated transparent Zcash (ZEC) deposits/withdrawals via our own inhouse operated infrastructure.

We have been for several months in direct conversations with supportive members of the Zcash ecosystem to better understand the general direction of Zcash and the plans the Zcash foundation has in mind for the future.

Once we felt sufficiently confident we committed the resources and our CTO "locked in" and made shielded ZEC deposits/withdrawals via our inhouse infrastructure possible within 2 days of committed & focused work.

### Time Period of Work Completion

September 2025

### Total Budget (USD)

10000

### Budget Breakdown

The aforementioned amount is mostly a suggestion based on some of the grant submissions we have seen for similar type of services (integration of shielded ZEC into an instant swap platform).

As the solution has been built and works in practice - and is not based on "future promises" - we assume this might be a justifiable amount, but we leave it up to the community to decide what they think is appropriate.

We build the solution because we believe in a sufficient market demand & possible ecosystem collaborations - we did not optimize our work for "grant application success".

We expect nothing, but are appreciative if the community finds our work valuable.



### Previous Funding

No

### Previous Funding Details

(none)

### Other Funding Sources

No

### Other Funding Sources Details

(none)

### Success Metrics

It is possible via our platform to instantly swap from/to shielded ZEC into any supported asset on BitcoinVN - without sign-up requirement.

Furthermore it is possible to bridge from shielded ZEC to transparent ZEC ( https://bitcoinvn.io/?deposit=zec&settle=zecshielded )

The platform also provides the ability to swap from/to alternative privacy options such as the Lightning Network, Monero etc - as well as most other common cryptocurrencies and stablecoins.

We have seen - at this early stage - a few dozen successful retail user transactions involving shielded ZEC, we aim to release more comprehensive statistics in the months to come as we gather more metrics involving ZEC swaps.

### Proof of completion

https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/bitcoinvn-zec-infrastructure-upgrade-q3-2025/52092/1

The service is publicly accessible for users as of right now.

(none)
